An empty result on a table with dates often means the table's **window**, the date range and grain it is set to show, does not cover the dates that hold values: writing dated values does not move the window, and a wrong window is fixed on the table itself. Two other causes are common: a member whose cells are all empty is hidden when the table hides empty members, and a member outside a formula's condition reads empty. Ask Ari to check the table's window before reworking its breakdown.","target":"dashboards/table-view-grammar","content_scope":"excerpt"},{"type":"text","record_type":"documentation","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/dashboards/build-and-format-tables","title":"Build and format a Table Block","context":"## How a Table Block is presented

Once a table calculates the right thing, ask Ari to adjust its presentation without touching the calculation:

* **Rename** the block's title.
* **Columns** — widths and whether the formula column is visible. Pinning a column so it stays beside the row names is a by-hand action from the column header; see [Work without Ari](/getting-started/build-by-hand#hide-resize-and-reorder).
* **Visibility** — hide or show specific rows or columns without deleting them.
* **Window** — change the shown date range or grain on an existing table.
* **Comparison** — show another Scenario, or an earlier period, alongside the baseline. See [Create and compare Scenarios](/scenarios/create-and-compare-scenarios).
* **Sort** — order an axis ascending, descending, or in a manual order you specify.
* **Formatting** — fill color, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, and row indent, applied to a whole row, a whole column, or a specific cell.
* **Orientation** — the same table read the other way, by moving an axis between rows and columns; the grain of every cell stays the same.","target":"dashboards/build-and-format-tables","content_scope":"excerpt"},{"type":"text","record_type":"documentation","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/formulas/agent-docs/create-and-update","title":"Create and update formulas as an agent","context":"## Set a table's window and grain

`window` is the table's own date range and grain. On a `create` it holds `start`, `end`, and `granularity`: a dated table names its grain, such as `MONTH`, and a timeless table names `NO_GRANULARITY`, as the example above does. On an `update`'s settings the range is `{"type": "ABSOLUTE", "start": …, "end": …}`. `start` and `end` accept a plain calendar date such as `2026-02-01` as well as a full timestamp, and create and update save the same window for either spelling. `{"inherit": true}` clears the table's own window. `update` with `grain` moves the table's Date columns to that grain, so a monthly table asked for `QUARTER` shows quarter columns and the receipt reports the moved Date column; a table whose Date header shows two grains at once, such as Year above Month, is refused a new grain.

A `values` write names each Date column by the start of its period at the table's grain. On a table with yearly columns, `2024-01`, `2024`, `FY2024`, and `2024-01-01` all write the 2024 cell; `2024-02` is refused as a date inside a YEAR period, and the refusal names the spelling that works. A period outside the table's window is refused with the window and the start or end that would hold it, such as "2025-12 is before this table's window 2026-01…2026-12; a window that starts 2025-12-01 holds it", and a call may set `window` and write the new periods together. A whole number such as `2026` also selects a number Dimension item printed `2026.0`, and a row renamed in the same request resolves under either name.

A JSON number in exponent form saves as the same value in plain decimal digits, so `1.5e-3` saves as `0.0015`; the formula grammar has no exponent literal. A number outside the 64-bit floating-point range is refused with "`<literal>` is outside the 64-bit floating-point range".

Dated inputs in `values` or `cell_updates`, and the periods a `readback` selects, leave the table's saved display window unchanged. A report that must show a requested start and end needs `window` set on the same call, or the table keeps showing its old range with the new months outside it; a readback of selected months proves those cells, not the displayed range.","target":"formulas/agent-docs/create-and-update","content_scope":"excerpt"},{"type":"text","record_type":"documentation","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/formulas/formula-reference/formula-errors-and-troubleshooting","title":"Formula errors and troubleshooting","context":"## A table cannot date an imported source

A Table Block that shows a Variable from an imported source by period needs to know which of the source's columns dates its rows: a date column the source contributes to the Model's Date, or a date column saved as the preferred time column of the Variables read from it. When the source has neither, the table stops calculating and reports:

```text theme={null}
Source "Payroll" (6077cf1b-…) has no date column to read it by. Give the source a date column, or set one of its date columns as the preferred time property ("Dated by") of the variables read from it.
```

Tell Ari which column dates the rows, and Ari saves it as the source's preferred time column, or add a date column at the source and sync again. A read that does not depend on Date still answers, such as `last` over the source's rows in a table with no Date axis. Ari receives the same message when it reads the table, so it can name the source to fix.","target":"formulas/formula-reference/formula-errors-and-troubleshooting","content_scope":"excerpt"},{"type":"text","record_type":"documentation","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/formulas/agent-docs/read-and-explain","title":"Read and explain formulas as an agent","context":"## Read a monthly table by quarter or year

`read` takes `grain: "QUARTER"` or `"YEAR"` to read a table's Date periods at a coarser grain than the saved table's own, without changing the table. Each period holds what the Model calculates at that grain: the Variable's time rollup (its base periods summed, closed, or averaged) or a timeless formula recomputed there. A Variable with neither reads `#NO_ROLLUP` in those cells, with one issue explaining that no rule computes it at that grain and that the values are in the table's own periods; the app shows such a cell as 0. A Scenario or time comparison read at a coarser grain still shows 0 there. The period columns come back `writable: false`, because their refs spell the date each period starts and would name the saved month column in a write. A table with no Date axis, or one already at that grain or coarser, refuses with the reason. Continuation cursors carry the grain.

```json theme={null}
{
  "scenario": "Main",
  "read": { "target": "Operating Plan", "rows": ["Bookings"], "grain": "YEAR" }
}
```

A period selector can also be spelled the way people write it, and it is read under each column's own grain: `2027` or `FY2027` selects a year column, `Q3 2026` or `2026 Q3` a quarter column, and `Mar 2026` a month column. `2027` never selects January of a monthly axis. The stored spelling, such as `2027-01`, still works everywhere.","target":"formulas/agent-docs/read-and-explain","content_scope":"excerpt"}]

[{"type":"text","record_type":"documentation","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/dashboards/share-pages-and-scenarios","title":"Share a Page and choose its Scenario","context":"## Know what a link allows

* Anyone with the link can **view** the Page. A link never grants editing, and it never makes someone a workspace administrator. A link only adds view access: a workspace member who opens it keeps the role and Page access they already have, including the right to edit, so a link is not a way to make a teammate read-only.
* The recipient does not need to sign in. There is no setting that requires a sign-in for an external link.
* A recipient who does sign in keeps the Pages shared with them attached to their account, which is why the app suggests **Sign in to hold on to the pages shared with you** to anonymous viewers.
* A link stays active until you turn it off in the sharing panel.

When someone needs to collaborate directly instead, ask Ari to invite them to the workspace; see [Workspace and team settings](/workspace-settings/team-and-workspace).","target":"dashboards/share-pages-and-scenarios","content_scope":"excerpt"},{"type":"text","record_type":"documentation","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/getting-started/build-by-hand","title":"Build and edit your Model by hand","context":"## Share a Page

The Page header has a **Share** button. Select it to create read-only external links under **External access**; each link opens without a sign-in and can carry its own **Shared scenario** and an optional **Require password** setting. **Turn off external link** stops a link and, by default, also removes the access of anyone who opened the Page through it. Everyone inside the workspace is an administrator and can already open every Page. See [Share a Page and choose its Scenario](/dashboards/share-pages-and-scenarios).","target":"getting-started/build-by-hand","content_scope":"excerpt"},{"type":"text","record_type":"documentation","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/dashboards/pages-and-blocks","title":"Pages and blocks","context":"## Organize a Page

Ask Ari to:

* Create a new Page, at the top level or nested under an existing one.
* Rename or move a Page, including reparenting it under a different Page.
* Create, reorder, or remove blocks on a Page.
* Move a block from one Page to another without losing its settings.

Because reordering an existing block preserves its configuration and ID, ask Ari to reorder a block rather than deleting and recreating it.

A Page Ari creates always gets an icon and an icon color. Ari picks a plain picture of what the Page is about and gives Pages on the same subject, and a subpage and its parent, the same accent color, so related Pages stand out together in the sidebar. Ask Ari to change either, or pick a new icon yourself from the Page header; see [Create, rename, and organize Pages](/getting-started/build-by-hand#create-rename-and-organize-pages).","target":"dashboards/pages-and-blocks","content_scope":"excerpt"},{"type":"text","record_type":"documentation","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/workspace-settings/team-and-workspace","title":"Workspace and team settings","context":"## Invite or remove workspace administrators

There is no team screen in Settings. Ask Ari, and when you have the required access it can:

* **Invite** someone as a workspace administrator. They receive an email invitation. Inviting an address whose invitation is still pending sends the email again, so ask Ari to resend rather than to cancel and re-invite.
* **Promote** an existing member to administrator. This changes their role and sends no invitation.
* **Remove** a member who has joined. Ari refuses to remove you or the workspace's last administrator.
* **Cancel** a pending invitation. Canceling and removing are separate actions: Ari refuses to cancel an invitation for someone who has already joined, and that person keeps their access, so a colleague who accepts while you are talking to Ari is never removed by mistake.

> Invite [dana@example.com](mailto:dana@example.com) to the workspace.

> Who has a pending invitation, and can you cancel the one for the old contractor?

Ari cannot invite someone with a lower role or revoke a share link. Ari can create a view-only share link to a Page; see [Share a Page and choose its Scenario](/dashboards/share-pages-and-scenarios).","target":"workspace-settings/team-and-workspace","content_scope":"excerpt"},{"type":"text","record_type":"documentation","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/getting-started/understand-your-workspace","title":"Understand your workspace","context":"## Use cfo.ai on a phone

A phone browser opens the same workspace at native scale, one surface at a time. The header's **Open navigation** button opens a drawer with the **Search** field, your chats, the Model section with its Pages, and Connections; picking a chat, a search result, or **New chat** closes it. A chat header offers **Open page panel** to read a Page beside the conversation, and a Page header offers **New chat**; **Back to chat** returns from a Page to the conversation.

Pages are read-only in this presentation, whatever your access: you can read tables and Canvas blocks, and a table's **Table block settings** menu offers only **Show formula bar** and **Show formula columns** beside **Mention table in chat**, but you cannot edit cells, add rows or blocks, or create Pages or Scenarios. An empty state says **Pages are read-only in this browser. Use Desktop Site to create a page.** Ask your browser for **Desktop Site** to get the desktop product, editing included, on the same device. A tablet gets the same read-only presentation unless it asks for the desktop site.","target":"getting-started/understand-your-workspace","content_scope":"excerpt"},{"type":"text","record_type":"documentation","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/ari/during-a-conversation","title":"Steer, stop, and approve during a chat","context":"## Manage your chats

The chat sidebar lists your conversations under **My sessions**, and any conversation someone else opened for you under **Shared with me**. Filter the list by **Active**, **Archived**, or **All**. Both sections keep their order, newest activity first, when you open a chat; a chat moves up only when something happens in it.

Open a conversation's menu to **Archive chat**, which hides it from the active list without deleting anything, or **Unarchive chat** to bring it back. A conversation you have not sent anything in yet offers **Discard chat** instead. You can also rename a conversation inline.

A conversation shared with you is read-only: the chat says **You can view this shared conversation, but can't send messages.** Start your own chat to ask Ari about what you see.","target":"ari/during-a-conversation","content_scope":"excerpt"},{"type":"text","record_type":"documentation","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/integrations/connect-and-sync-data","title":"Connect and sync your data","context":"## Ask Ari to connect an MCP server or API

A workspace administrator can also have Ari set up an MCP server or an API from the chat, for example "Connect PostHog's MCP server." **Add with Ari** on the **MCP** or **API** tab of the connection manager, or on the **MCP** or **APIs** tab under **Settings → Connections**, opens a chat that starts the same way, asking which provider to connect and what you want to do with it. Ari reads the provider's official documentation, then posts a card headed **Connect \[service]** with the service's logo, its address, how it signs in, and a **Provider documentation** link. In this chat flow an MCP server signs in with OAuth or a **Bearer token**; a server that needs an API key header is added from the **Add MCP server** dialog instead. An API uses a **Bearer API key**, a named header, an **API key as Basic username**, or **No authentication**. The card carries no credentials, and Ari never asks for a key in the chat.

Select **Connect**. A service that uses OAuth opens its sign-in window; one that takes a token or key shows a secure field on the card, and what you type there goes to cfo.ai's connection service, not to Ari or into the conversation. The card reads **Connecting…**, then **Checking connection…** while cfo.ai confirms that the server's tools answer or that the API's endpoints loaded, then **Connected** for a server or **API saved** for an API. On a failure it offers **Retry**, and a retry keeps a connection that was already saved; **Cancel** stops the setup. A member who cannot manage connections sees **A workspace admin must connect this service.**

When the provider refuses cfo.ai's sign-in address, the message **The provider must approve cfo.ai's sign-in URL to connect.** appears on the card, and in the **Add MCP server** dialog in Settings. Trying again cannot fix that; the provider has to allow cfo.ai's callback address first. A provider that rejects the registration for another reason is named as the one that refused, and a temporary failure still asks you to try connecting again. Once a server is connected, Ari gives it 45 seconds to answer when a chat turn or the Settings page lists its tools; a server that stays silent is reported as unavailable for that turn, and the other servers' tools still work.

Once the card completes, Ari continues in the same chat: it checks the connection's tools or endpoints and, for an API, verifies the key with a documented read before relying on it. **API saved** means the definition parsed, not that the key works. An OAuth provider that needs a preregistered app, and an API that signs in with a username and password or with a key in the query string, cannot be set up this way; Ari says so instead of collecting the secret.","target":"integrations/connect-and-sync-data","content_scope":"excerpt"},{"type":"text","record_type":"documentation","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/dashboards/charts-and-custom-visualizations","title":"Charts and custom visualizations","context":"## Live data, not a snapshot

A custom visual reads from named Model data views using the same Variables and Dimensions you would use to build a Table Block. The chart updates as its underlying Model values change.

A visual receives each Variable's own kind of value: numbers, text such as a customer code or a currency, dates, and true/false values. A table of labels or invoice dates can drive a visual directly, without a numeric stand-in. An empty cell or a calculation error reaches the visual as no value.

A visual resolves its data in the Page's Scenario unless one of its data views names another saved Scenario. A Canvas block can read up to three Scenarios, so one block can chart Main, an Upside, and a Downside side by side; Ari's **Scenario comparison** template is built this way. Every read of another Scenario checks that the viewer can read that Scenario; a viewer who cannot gets no data for that view. A Table Block offers a saved side-by-side comparison too. See [Create and compare Scenarios](/scenarios/create-and-compare-scenarios).

A button inside a visual can do a few things when you click it: open another Page or block in your workspace, including a Page or block Ari named in a chat; prepare a draft message for Ari that you review before sending; or start a new chat that sends its message at once, for example to ask Ari to present a saved Guide. That new chat opens even when the Page has not finished loading the block's name; in that case the message goes without a reference to the block.

When Ari checks a visual it built, it renders the block once per light and dark theme at a width of 1200 px with the block's saved state, and reads the errors and warnings from those renders. It does not click buttons, type into inputs, follow links, or launch Guides, so what those do is not checked, and neither is the layout at other widths.","target":"dashboards/charts-and-custom-visualizations","content_scope":"excerpt"},{"type":"text","record_type":"documentation","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/agent-instructions","title":"Agent instructions","context":"## Shape each call as one action block

A multi-action tool takes exactly one block named for the action, with that action's fields inside it. There is no flat `action` field. For example, read a saved table with `inspect_table_blocks`:

```json theme={null}
{ "read": { "target": "Operating Plan" } }
```

and set a row's formula with `edit_table_blocks`:

```json theme={null}
{
  "update": {
    "target": "Operating Plan",
    "row_updates": [
      {
        "rows": ["Gross Margin"],
        "default_formulas": { "forecast": { "formula": "iferror(`Gross Profit` / Revenue, 0)" } }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

A row on a dated table takes `default_formulas` with `actuals`, `forecast`, or both; a row on a timeless table takes `formula`. Several dependent tables can go in one `create` as a `tables` list. A `delete` that lists `variables` or `dimensions` removes only those objects; when other formulas, blocks, or settings read one, the delete is refused until `force: true` is set, on the delete to cover every listed entry or on one entry to cover that entry alone. Fields that every action accepts, such as `scenario`, sit beside the block, and `scenario` is also accepted inside it. Copy names and `Name#hex` references from an inspection result instead of inventing IDs. See [Create and update formulas as an agent](/formulas/agent-docs/create-and-update) for the full shapes.

A Canvas block is named in the call that makes it: `edit_canvas_blocks` `create` requires `page`, `title`, and `source`. The reference the receipt prints, such as `Pipeline by stage#a74`, keeps naming the block in later `edit_pages` calls even after a rename. Before writing a Canvas block, call `inspect_canvas_library` with a `list` block whose `query` is a few search words, such as `"slider chart kpi"`; an entry matches when any one word appears in its title, description, tags, or aliases. Then `read` the entries you plan to use. One `read` takes up to 16 targets, so a template and the components it needs come back in one call. A Canvas write that no browser rendered returns a `render_unverified` warning naming `validate_code_blocks`, the tool that renders saved blocks in a browser and reports errors and a screenshot; a write sent with `validate: true` carries that browser result under `validation` instead. The result's `observed` sentence states what the check saw: each block rendered once per theme, with its saved state, in a 1200 px wide frame, so clicks, typing, links, and guide launches did not run and the layout at other widths is unseen. One call renders up to 8 blocks; a batch that reads a lot of calculated data is split into several renders, a single block over 20 MiB of data is refused by name, and a render run that failed returns the error code `browser_validation_unavailable` with `transient: true` and a message that names the validator stage that failed and the error behind it, so the same call can be sent again. To change part of a saved block, `edit_canvas_blocks` `update` takes `source_patches`, a list of exact `old` to `new` text replacements applied in order, each of which must occur exactly once; the block saves only when every patch applies, and `source` replaces the whole component instead. A Canvas `navigate` accepts a page or block reference in the form tool results return, and opens it the way a link chip does. `inspect_history` `changelog` takes `search` to find entries by text in the headline or in the names of the objects they changed, newest first, and reports how many entries it read in `entries_searched`. A dataset row carries each Variable's own value: a finite number, text, an ISO day such as `2026-01-30` for a date, `"true"` or `"false"` for a boolean, and `null` for an empty cell or a calculation error. Source may name a fixed color; the write saves it and its result's `source_notes` names the first one and says that colors from `theme.tokens`, `theme.design`, or `--cb-*` CSS variables follow the viewer's light or dark mode instead.

In `edit_pages`, a block action names its page with `page`; `add_text` may omit it, adding to the page in view instead, and is refused with "no target page" when nothing is in view. `reorder_blocks` still takes the page it arranges as `target`.","target":"agent-instructions","content_scope":"excerpt"},{"type":"text","record_type":"documentation","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/ari/meet-ari","title":"Meet Ari","context":"## You remain in control

Some steps still require you. You approve sign-ins for external systems, review important or destructive changes, and revoke share links from the Page's **Share** control.

Ari works within your workspace access and the available connected data. When a key input is missing or an assumption affects the answer, Ari should explain what it knows and what still needs your decision.","target":"ari/meet-ari","content_scope":"excerpt"}]

{"complete":true,"content":"# Understand Scenarios

> Understand Main, editable Scenarios, automatic inheritance, Snapshots, comparisons, and Scenario history.

A Scenario lets you explore a different version of your Model without changing Main. Use one when a pricing decision, hiring plan, financing event, or other assumption needs its own saved alternative.

## Main and child Scenarios

Every Model has one **Main** Scenario. Main holds the numbers your team treats as the current plan, and it's what most Pages show by default.

An editable Scenario branches from Main. Changes you make in that Scenario, such as updating a formula or adjusting a headcount assumption, apply there until you decide whether to merge them into Main.

Child Scenarios are useful for:

* Modeling a what-if question, like a hiring freeze or a pricing change, without disturbing the plan everyone else is working from.
* Drafting next quarter's Forecast before you're ready to share it.
* Comparing two versions of the same plan side by side.

## How a Scenario stays current

An editable Scenario automatically inherits updates from Main while keeping its own changes. For example, refreshed accounting data can appear in both Main and your hiring-plan Scenario, while the alternative hiring assumption remains specific to the Scenario.

Connected source data is shared, except with a Snapshot, which stops receiving integration updates. A Scenario changes the Model rules, values, and presentation that differ from Main; it does not create a private copy of an integration.

A Scenario stores only the values that differ from the Scenario it branched from. If you ask Ari to set a value that the Scenario already inherits, nothing is saved: Ari reports that the cell keeps following Main and changes when Main changes. Give the Scenario a different value when you want it to hold still while Main moves.

## What a Scenario would merge in

Before merging a Scenario, ask Ari what would change. Ari can inspect the saved change summary and explain which Variables, formulas, values, Pages, or tables differ from Main.

Merging applies the Scenario's changes to Main, the Scenario it branched from, and removes the merged Scenario. Review the affected changes before approving the merge. Undoing the merge from the version history brings the merged Scenario back.

## Snapshots preserve a point in time

A **Snapshot** pins Main or an editable Scenario to a specific point in its history. After that point, nothing from the source flows into it:

* **Integration updates.** When QuickBooks or another source syncs, Main updates and the Snapshot keeps the numbers it had.
* **Edits to the source.** A formula, assumption, or hard-coded value someone changes in Main later stays out of the Snapshot.
* **Table setup.** Later changes to a Table Block's settings or column widths in the source do not carry over.

Use a Snapshot to preserve a submitted budget, board-reporting baseline, or the plan your team approved at a particular date.

To create one, ask Ari and name the Scenario to preserve, or take it yourself: open the Scenario picker while viewing the Scenario and select **Take snapshot**, or open **Version history** and choose **Take snapshot here** on the entry to pin. The **Take snapshot** dialog suggests the name **\[Scenario] snapshot** and saves with **Create snapshot**. Taking a Snapshot yourself needs permission to create Scenarios, and neither control is offered on a phone or while you are viewing a Snapshot.

A Snapshot also has these limits:

* **A Snapshot is not read-only.** You and Ari can still type hard-coded values over its numbers, and those edits save. Treat a Snapshot as a copy your team agrees not to touch.
* **A Snapshot cannot be merged** into Main.
* **A Snapshot cannot be reverted** to an earlier point, and you cannot take a Snapshot of another Snapshot. To pin an earlier point of a Scenario, use **Take snapshot here** on that entry in the Scenario's version history.

## Review and reverse changes

cfo.ai keeps a version history of every write to a Scenario. Open it with the **Version history** control in the Page header. Each entry's actions menu offers **Copy link to version** and these ways to reverse a change:

* **Undo this change** for a specific change or a related batch of changes. An entry the Scenario inherited from Main cannot be undone from the child.
* **Redo this change** on an entry you undid.
* **Restore this version** to return the Scenario to an earlier point in its history. This rolls back every later change, so review the impact first. The restore itself becomes a history entry you can undo. Ari calls the same action a revert.

Ask Ari to show you the history, or to explain what changed between two points in time, before deciding to undo or restore.

## Next steps

See [Create and compare Scenarios](/scenarios/create-and-compare-scenarios) for how to branch a new Scenario and view it alongside Main on a Table Block.","content_scope":"full_page","record_type":"documentation","target":"scenarios/understand-scenarios","type":"text","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/scenarios/understand-scenarios"}

{"complete":true,"content":"# Create and compare Scenarios

> Branch a new Scenario, show it alongside Main on a Table Block, and ask Ari to compare the two.

Use a Scenario when you want to save an alternative plan while keeping Main unchanged. Use a saved Table Block comparison to view the two versions side by side.

## Create a Scenario

Ask Ari to create an editable Scenario from Main:

> Create a Scenario called Hiring Freeze from Main.

You can also start without Ari: open the Scenario picker, the **Main Scenario** control in the sidebar's **Model** section, then select **Create scenario**.

The Scenario inherits Main and keeps any changes you make separately. Work inside it by updating Variables, changing formulas, adjusting headcount, or reorganizing Pages.

An editable Scenario is created from Main. If you need to preserve another Scenario exactly as it exists now, create a Snapshot instead: ask Ari, or select **Take snapshot** in the Scenario picker while viewing that Scenario. A Snapshot stops receiving integration updates and other later changes, but its values can still be overwritten. See [Snapshots preserve a point in time](/scenarios/understand-scenarios#snapshots-preserve-a-point-in-time).

## Compare Scenarios on a Table Block

A Table Block can show one or more Scenarios beside its baseline. Ask Ari to add a comparison, and choose:

* **Which Scenarios** to show alongside the baseline.
* **Layout** — compared Scenarios can sit in columns or in rows.
* **Measures** — the raw value, the delta, the percent difference, or some combination.

A Table Block compares across Scenarios or across a shifted time period, but those two comparison modes cannot be active together. The table can still show ordinary monthly columns while comparing Scenarios.

## Ask Ari about existing Scenario values

If a saved table already contains the relevant information, ask Ari to compare what is visible in each Scenario:

> How does Operating Expense in the Hiring Freeze Scenario compare with Main for next quarter?

If the comparison needs a new saved layout, Ari can add a comparison to a Table Block or create a separate analysis table when you authorize that change.

## Review before merging

Before merging, ask Ari what would change. Review the affected Model content and remember that a successful merge applies those changes to Main and removes the merged Scenario.

{"complete":true,"content":"# Connect the cfo.ai MCP server

> Connect Claude Code, Codex, or another MCP client to cfo.ai, authorize access, and choose the correct workspace.

cfo.ai runs its own MCP server at `https://api.cfo.ai/mcp`. Any AI client that supports remote MCP servers can connect, including Claude Code and Codex.

The connection lets an external agent use the same workspace tools Ari uses. Those tools can inspect your Model and, when authorized, change live Pages, Scenarios, Variables, Dimensions, and formulas.

You, Ari, and the external agent share the same Model. Work created through the connection remains visible in your cfo.ai workspace, where you can inspect the assumptions, edit the result, or continue the work with Ari.

Setup below covers Claude Code and Codex.

## Before you start

You need a cfo.ai account with access to the intended workspace. If you do not have one yet, sign up at [app.cfo.ai](https://app.cfo.ai) and complete the required account setup first.

## Claude Code

<Steps>
  <Step title="Add the MCP server">
    Open a terminal and add cfo.ai as an MCP server:

    ```bash theme={null}
    claude mcp add --transport http cfoai https://api.cfo.ai/mcp
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Start Claude Code">
    ```bash theme={null}
    claude
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Open the MCP menu">
    Type `/mcp` and look for `cfoai` in the list of servers.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Authenticate">
    Select `cfoai`, then choose **Authenticate**. A browser window opens. Make sure you're logged into your cfo.ai account before approving the connection.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Codex

<Steps>
  <Step title="Add the MCP server">
    Open a terminal and add cfo.ai as an MCP server:

    ```bash theme={null}
    codex mcp add cfoai --url https://api.cfo.ai/mcp
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Authenticate">
    ```bash theme={null}
    codex mcp login cfoai
    ```

    A browser window opens. Make sure you're logged into your cfo.ai account before approving the connection.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Verify">
    Start Codex with `codex`, then type `/mcp` to confirm `cfoai` is connected.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Other MCP clients

Any harness that supports remote MCP servers can connect. Add `https://api.cfo.ai/mcp` as a custom connector or MCP server in your agent's settings, then sign in with your cfo.ai account when the browser prompt appears.

## Choose the correct workspace

If your account belongs to one workspace, the connection can use it automatically. If your account belongs to several workspaces, ask the agent to call `list_orgs`, select the correct workspace by its ID or slug, and pass that value as `org_id` on each later tool call.

Writes apply to the selected live workspace. Use a Scenario when you want an external agent to work on an alternative plan without changing Main.

## What the connection exposes

The server publishes Ari's public workspace tools, such as `inspect_table_blocks`, `edit_table_blocks`, `inspect_pages`, `edit_pages`, `inspect_canvas_library`, `edit_canvas_blocks`, `inspect_scenarios`, `edit_scenarios`, `edit_dimension_mappings`, `inspect_integrations`, `edit_integrations`, `inspect_skills`, `edit_triggers`, and `inspect_documentation`, plus `list_orgs`. Tools that only make sense inside the cfo.ai app, such as the ones that ask you a question in chat or play a Guide, are not published.

A tool with several actions takes exactly one block named for the action, for example `{"read": {"target": "Operating Plan"}}` for `inspect_table_blocks`. The [agent instructions](/agent-instructions) show the shape.

## Agent instructions

Rather have your agent do this? Copy this prompt into it. Your agent will walk you through everything, from sign-up to a working connection, and tell you when it needs you:

```text theme={null}
Set up cfo.ai for me. Fetch https://docs.cfo.ai/agent-instructions.md and follow the instructions there. If I don't have a cfo.ai account yet, walk me through creating one first, then connect the cfo.ai MCP server to this harness and verify it's working.
```

If you are an AI agent reading this page: fetch `https://docs.cfo.ai/agent-instructions.md` and follow it.

Once authenticated, your agent can call the available cfo.ai tools directly. If authentication fails, check that you are signed in to the correct cfo.ai account and have access to the intended workspace.","content_scope":"full_page","record_type":"documentation","target":"integrations/mcp-server","type":"text","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/integrations/mcp-server"}

{"complete":true,"content":"# Share a Page and choose its Scenario

> Create a read-only external link to a Page, choose the Scenario it shows, add a password when needed, and turn a link off.

Use a Page's **Share** control when you want someone outside the workspace to view a report, dashboard, or analysis. External links are read-only and open without a sign-in, so the recipient sees the Page as it is when they open it, in the Scenario you chose.

Everyone inside the workspace is an administrator and can already open every Page, so sharing is for people outside it: an investor, a board member, an accountant, or a teammate who does not need a workspace seat.

## Create an external link

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the Page">
    Navigate to the Page you want to share.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Select Share">
    Select **Share** in the Page header. The panel names the Page so you can confirm you are sharing the intended report.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Choose the Scenario">
    Use the **Shared scenario** selector on the link to choose the Scenario it
    shows. This matters when the same Page presents different results in Main
    and in an alternative Scenario.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Create the link">
    Under **External access**, select **Create link**. Turn on **Require password**
    when the recipient should enter a password before viewing the Page, and copy
    and share that password separately from the link.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Copy the link">
    Select **Copy external link** and send it to the intended recipient.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Share several Pages through one link

One external link can open more than one Page in the same Scenario, so a board packet with a summary, a profit and loss statement, and a headcount view opens as one link. The Page you share from is the landing page. Ask Ari for a link like this; the **Share** panel's link rows then list every Page the link opens.

> Create a view-only link to the Board summary Page that also opens the Cash forecast and Headcount plan Pages.

Ari returns the link's address. The link works for anyone who holds it until you revoke it in **Share**, and creating it does not change the Model.

## Know what a link allows

* Anyone with the link can **view** the Page. A link never grants editing, and it never makes someone a workspace administrator. A link only adds view access: a workspace member who opens it keeps the role and Page access they already have, including the right to edit, so a link is not a way to make a teammate read-only.
* The recipient does not need to sign in. There is no setting that requires a sign-in for an external link.
* A recipient who does sign in keeps the Pages shared with them attached to their account, which is why the app suggests **Sign in to hold on to the pages shared with you** to anonymous viewers.
* A link stays active until you turn it off in the sharing panel.

When someone needs to collaborate directly instead, ask Ari to invite them to the workspace; see [Workspace and team settings](/workspace-settings/team-and-workspace).

## Turn a link off

The sharing panel lists active links. Select **Turn off external link** on a link when the recipient should no longer be able to use it. The confirmation has **Also remove access already granted by this link** checked by default, which also removes the access of anyone who opened the Page through that link; clear it to let them keep their access. Create a new link if the required Scenario or password changes. Turning a link off is only possible from the panel, not through Ari.

## What you cannot share yet

Only Pages have a **Share** control today. Scenarios, conversations, individual Variables, and formulas are not shareable on their own; share the Page that shows them.

## Related

* [Pages and blocks](/dashboards/pages-and-blocks)
* [Understand Scenarios](/scenarios/understand-scenarios)

{"complete":true,"content":"# What Ari remembers

> Learn what Ari saves between conversations, the difference between your private memory and the workspace's shared memory, and how to see or remove a saved fact.

Ari can carry facts from one conversation into the next, so you do not have to restate how you like tables formatted, which Scenario is your working plan, or what a business term means at your company. This memory is deliberate: Ari saves a fact when you ask it to or when you state a lasting preference, not a transcript of everything you said.

## Two scopes

Every saved fact belongs to one of two scopes:

* **Your memory** is private to you. Ari reads it in your conversations only. Use it for how you personally like to work, such as "show me quarters, not months" or "I run the sales team."
* **Workspace memory** is shared with everyone in the workspace. Use it for facts about the company that every teammate and every conversation should respect, such as "our fiscal year starts in February" or "Bookings means signed contract value."

A fact never moves scope on its own. If Ari replaces a fact with a newer version, the new one keeps the scope of the old one.

## Tell Ari what to remember

Say it plainly, and say who it is for.

> Remember that I prefer ending cash shown in thousands.

> For the whole workspace, remember that "Enterprise" means contracts above \$50,000 a year.

Ari can save several related facts at once, and it can take a longer document, such as a page of company conventions, and save the facts it finds there. Ask Ari to confirm what it saved.

## See what Ari knows

> What do you remember about me?

> What has the workspace taught you about how we report?

Ari lists the saved facts in the scope you asked about, or in both when you do not say.

## Ask Ari to forget

> Forget that I prefer quarters.

Ari removes the fact from the scope it lives in and confirms. Only that fact goes; other facts Ari saved from the same request stay. When the fact you name is one Ari drew from several saved facts, Ari asks which of them to forget. A workspace fact is removed for everyone, so say which scope you mean when the same fact could live in both.

## Memory is not chat history

Saved memory is separate from Ari's ability to look back at earlier conversations. Ari can still reference a past chat when you point it there. When it looks back on its own, it sees each earlier chat under the title you see in the sidebar, including one you renamed, so it can pick the conversation that defined a term. A shared conversation stays readable to the people it was shared with. Memory is the short list of facts Ari applies without being asked.

{"complete":true,"content":"# Build a financial model of your business

> Build a dynamic financial model that reflects how your business earns revenue, spends money, hires, and changes over time.

A useful financial Model is a dynamic simulation of how your business works. Change a hiring date, growth assumption, or price, and you can see how the decision affects revenue, expenses, and cash over time.

You and Ari work from the same Model. Ari can build or update it, and you can inspect the formulas, change assumptions, and keep using the result after the conversation ends.

## Start with how the business works

Identify the real things and events that change your results.

* A subscription company may need customers, plans, seats, new contracts, expansion, churn, billing, and collections.
* A services business may need clients, projects, team members, billable time, utilization, and project start and end dates.
* A retail or physical-product business may need products, orders, inventory, purchase timing, fulfillment, and returns.

Tell Ari what creates revenue, what creates cost, and what decisions the Model should help you make.

> We sell annual software subscriptions. Model customers by segment and plan, include new business and churn, and connect hiring and operating expenses to our cash forecast.

## Keep meaningful business detail

Use Dimensions for the categories that change how you analyze the business. Common examples include Customer, Product, Department, Employee, Region, Entity, and Date.

The right level of detail depends on the decision. If churn differs by customer segment, keep customer segment. If payroll depends on a person's start date, compensation, and department, keep the employee-level detail behind the department total.

One real business category should map to one shared Dimension wherever possible. For example, Department should mean the same thing when data comes from accounting and HR.

## Connect source data and assumptions

Actuals come from the accounting, HR, CRM, spreadsheet, database, or file sources you connect. Assumptions describe what should happen next when the future cannot be observed directly.

Useful assumptions are named, visible, and easy to change. Examples include conversion rate, planned hiring, price increases, payment timing, and monthly churn.

When source data is incomplete, Ari can still build a forecast from explicit assumptions. Ask Ari to identify which values came from a source and which values were assumed.

## Make time part of the model

Every business changes across time. Set the date range and grain that match the question, such as months for a 12-month operating plan or weeks for a near-term cash forecast.

**Last close** separates closed Actuals from the Forecast. A Variable can use imported data in Actuals and a planning formula in Forecast while keeping the same business meaning across both ranges.

For example:

```text theme={null}
`Ending Customers` = `Beginning Customers` + `New Customers` - `Churned Customers`
```

```text theme={null}
`Subscription Revenue` = Customers * `Average Subscription Price`
```

The `=` in these examples explains the business relationship. When entering a formula for a selected Variable, enter the expression to the right of `=`.

## Build one connected system

Revenue, headcount, expenses, balance-sheet activity, and cash should agree with each other. A hiring plan should affect payroll. Changes in sales should affect recognized revenue and collections. The cash forecast should reflect the timing of the underlying inflows and outflows.

The same Model can appear in a hiring plan, cash forecast, or board report without becoming three disconnected copies. A business value keeps its meaning wherever you or Ari inspect it.

Organize the results into Pages and Table Blocks, then ask Ari to verify that important totals reconcile across the Model.

> Check that the department payroll totals match the employee detail, and show how the hiring plan changes ending cash.

## Test decisions in a Scenario

Keep Main as your working baseline. Create a Scenario when you want to explore a different price, growth rate, hiring plan, or financing decision without changing that baseline.

> Create a Scenario where enterprise churn falls by two percentage points and show the effect on revenue and cash over the next year.

{"complete":true,"content":"# Interactive Guides

> Build a step-by-step walkthrough that spotlights specific Pages, blocks, or cells for onboarding or analysis.

A **Guide** is a saved, interactive walkthrough that spotlights parts of your workspace, one step at a time, with a coachmark of explanatory text at each stop. Use a Guide to onboard a new team member, walk someone through an analysis, or narrate a feature.

## Guide modes

* **Tour** — a step-by-step feature or onboarding walkthrough. The default mode. Its card shows progress, **Back**, **Next**, **Done** on the last step, and **Skip tour**.
* **Walkthrough** — an analysis, like board-meeting prep, with softer wording: **Continue**, **Done**, and **Exit walkthrough**.
* **Explain** — a single on-demand spotlight rather than a multi-step sequence, closed with one **Got it** button.

When Ari starts a tour or walkthrough, the chat shows a **Start tour** or **Start walkthrough** button so you choose when it begins; an explanation opens at once. A button in a Canvas block can also ask Ari for a saved Guide: it starts a new chat that sends the request at once, and the Guide then follows the same rule, an explanation opening right away and a tour or walkthrough waiting for its **Start tour** or **Start walkthrough** button in that chat.

## What a step can spotlight

Each step targets one of:

* A **named** UI element, like a sidebar toggle.
* A **block** on a Page.
* A single **cell**, a whole **row**, or a whole **column** on a Table Block, addressed by the Variables and Dimension items that identify it — including a Scenario comparison column.
* A **Canvas element** — one declared element inside a Canvas block, such as a KPI tile the Canvas source marks with a stable ID.
* **None** — a centered narration step with no on-screen target, useful for an introduction or a transition between sections.

A step whose target is not on screen is skipped, unless that target lives on another Page, in which case the Guide opens that Page first.

## Create a Guide

Ask Ari to save a new Guide with a title and its steps in order. For a Guide that targets blocks or cells, Ari uses the Scenario you're currently viewing so the targets and numbers line up when the Guide launches. Give each step a title and body, or richer content combining a heading, a label, and paragraphs. A step can carry a short readable key, such as `roster`, so you can ask Ari to start the Guide at that step later.

## Run a Guide

Ask Ari to start a saved Guide by name, or to start it at a named step. Once running, ask Ari to move to the next or previous step, jump to a specific step, or dismiss it early.

When you start a Guide from the floating chat window over a full-screen Page, the chat moves out of the way of whatever a step spotlights and keeps clear of the coachmark, then returns to where you had it when the Guide ends. On a small screen where no position clears the spotlight, the chat hides for the rest of that Guide and comes back when the Guide ends; your conversation and any half-typed message are kept.

## Update or remove a Guide

Ask Ari to replace a Guide's title and steps, or delete one you no longer need.

{"complete":true,"content":"# Billing and plan

> Check your plan, AI usage, and integration entitlements through Ari, and find where to make changes in Settings.

Ari can read your workspace's billing status directly, so you don't need to leave the conversation to check your plan or usage. Ari can't change billing itself — every answer points you to the specific Settings section to make the actual change.

## What Ari can tell you

Ask Ari about:

* **Plan** — your current plan, price, status, renewal date, and any scheduled change.
* **Usage** — your monthly AI usage as a percentage of the plan's allotment, your extra-usage balance, whether auto-reload is on, and your spending limit.
* **Integrations** — how many standard and premium connections your plan allows, and how many you're using. See [Integrations Directory](/integrations/integrations-directory) for what counts as standard vs. premium.
* **Available plans** — the tiers cfo.ai offers and what each includes.

Ari reports AI usage as a percentage and money as dollar amounts, since that's how the workspace's own billing data is expressed.

AI usage covers Ari's own model calls and the images Ari generates in a chat when you ask for one; a higher-quality image costs more. A workspace with no spendable usage left gets the usual pause before any image is requested.

## Plans

Open **Settings → Billing** to see the plans and switch between them. The plan cards show the current prices and limits for your workspace; the shape of each plan is:

* **Free** — start with your own data. It comes with a one-time allotment of AI credits that does not replenish, accepts CSV uploads as the only data source, and needs no card.
* **Starter** — build and run the finance model. Standard AI usage that resets monthly, five standard integrations, a ceiling on synced rows, the MCP server and Slack app, proactive alerts and Triggers, unlimited Models and Scenarios, and one dedicated workspace.
* **Growth** — everything in Starter with a multiple of the AI usage, more integrations, and a higher synced-row ceiling.
* **Enterprise** — custom pricing and AI credits. Adds premium integrations, including NetSuite and data warehouses, multiple workspaces, SSO / SAML, priority support, and a dedicated Forward Deployed Finance Partner with a shared Slack channel. The card opens a conversation with sales rather than switching the plan.

If your card is declined when you add it or pay, the form repeats the card provider's reason and adds **Check your payment details or try a different card.**

Use the **Monthly** / **Annual** toggle to compare cadences. Annual is selected by default when you first choose a paid plan and shows the saving against monthly billing. A paid plan starts with a 14-day free trial: select **Start free trial** on the card. Nothing is charged when the trial starts, and the card shows the price that applies per month after the trial. When you sign up, the plan page says **\$0 today. Cancel anytime before it ends and you won’t be charged, and you still get all 14 days free.** The **Add a payment method** dialog names the date to cancel by. Canceling during the trial does not cut it short.

Plans differ in how many connections of each class you can hold, not in what a connection does. File uploads never count toward the integration limit, and neither do the API and MCP connections Ari calls live; see [API and MCP connections do not sync](/integrations/integrations-directory#api-and-mcp-connections-do-not-sync).

## Usage settings

**Settings → Usage** shows your included AI usage, extra usage, data, and integrations, with three views for managing spend:

* **Spend limit** — a monthly cap on extra usage. Raise or remove it if a purchase is being blocked.
* **Buy credits** — add a one-time amount to your purchased usage balance.
* **Auto-reload** — keep the balance topped up automatically. Turn on **Auto-reload**, then set **When the balance falls below** an amount, **add** a reload amount, and **Save**. Auto-reload needs a default payment method in Billing first. The balance line reads **Auto-reload on**, **off**, or **paused**; it pauses after a failed payment until you update the payment method or buy credits.

## Who can see and change billing

Every member of a workspace can open **Billing** and **Usage**, see the plan and the numbers, change the plan, buy credits, and edit the spend limit or auto-reload, because every member is an administrator. Some workspaces are billed outside the app and show no Billing section at all.

A plan is priced for the workspace, not for each person in it, so inviting another administrator does not change what you pay. What the plan buys — your included AI usage and your standard and premium connection slots — is shared by everyone in the workspace.

## Changing your plan or limits

Ask Ari where to go, and it will point you to the right section in Settings. Ari won't quote you a specific price for a plan change, since Settings shows the exact number at confirmation, and pricing can vary by workspace.

When you choose your first paid plan, the plan cards open on **Annual** pricing. The toggle names the saving, such as **Annual — save 20%**; switch it to **Monthly** to see month-to-month prices.

## During your trial

While a workspace is on a trial and has not paid its first invoice, a banner above the workspace reads **Need a hand with cfo.ai?** with a **Talk to our Forward Deployed team** link to book a call. Select the **Dismiss** control (the ✕ at the right) to hide the banner for the rest of the day; it returns the next day until the first invoice is paid.

If you cancel during the trial, the trial still runs to its end, and the workspace then returns to the plan chooser rather than closing. The paid plans there start without another trial, because a workspace gets one trial.

### Start the paid plan before the trial ends

There is one self-serve way to end a trial early, and it appears only after the workspace has used all the AI usage included with the trial. A banner above the workspace then reads **You’ve used all the AI usage included with your trial** and carries a **Start paid plan** button. Select it, confirm, and cfo.ai ends the trial, charges the card on file, and refreshes your included AI usage for a new billing cycle. **Settings → Billing** has no separate control for this, so a workspace that still has trial usage left waits for the trial to end on its own.

Dismissing that banner hides it for the rest of the trial, not only for the day. If you dismissed it and still want to start the paid plan now, select **Support** in the navigation at the top of these docs.

## Cancel your subscription

There is no way to pause a subscription and pick it up later. Canceling is the only stop. It stops the billing and leaves your data in place rather than deleting the Model, and when the term ends the workspace returns to the plan chooser until someone picks a plan again. Deleting a workspace or an account is a separate request; see [Workspace and team settings](/workspace-settings/team-and-workspace).

Open **Settings → Billing**, find **Cancel subscription**, and select **Cancel**. The dialog asks why you are canceling and names the date through which service runs: a paid plan stays active until the end of the current plan term and is not charged again, and a trial stays active until it ends, with no charge.

You can undo the cancellation any time before that date. Open the plan chooser in **Settings → Billing** and keep your current plan or choose another one; either one calls the cancellation off.

## If AI usage runs out

When the workspace has no spendable AI usage remaining, Ari explains the account state and further requests are paused until usage is restored.

A workspace administrator can review the balance, purchase additional usage when available, or adjust auto-reload and monthly spending settings. A teammate without billing access should contact a workspace administrator.

If a monthly spending cap is preventing a purchase, adjust the applicable limit in Usage settings before trying again.

{"complete":true,"content":"# Save a workflow as a Skill

> Teach Ari a repeatable process once, as a Skill, so it activates automatically the next time the situation comes up.

A **Skill** is a saved process that tells Ari how to handle a recurring situation: what steps to take, what conventions to follow, and when to activate at all. Once saved, Ari activates a Skill on its own when a request matches its trigger condition — you don't need to reference it by name.

## Built-in and saved Skills

cfo.ai ships with built-in Skills covering common workflows. Your workspace can also hold its own saved Skills, written for how your team specifically works. Ask Ari to list what's available, including a search by name, to see both together.

## Turn on a built-in Skill

Some built-in Skills are off until you turn them on. Open **Settings → Skills** and find **Built-in skills** below your custom Skills. Turn on the switch next to a Skill to use it.

* **Model audit** — checks that the formulas, mappings, and statements hold together, and that the Model ties to the ledger and the bank. Ari writes a short audit page with live checks. Use it before the board or investors see the Model.
* **Flash report** — reads the current month before the books close. Actuals, committed spend, and estimates stay separate. Use it to answer "where are we this month?"

A switch applies to everyone in the workspace. cfo.ai keeps these Skills up to date, so you can't edit them.

## Create a Skill with Ari

The fastest way to make a Skill is to build it with Ari. You describe the workflow in plain words, and Ari writes and saves the Skill for you.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open Build with Ari">
    Go to **Settings → Skills** and select **Build with Ari**. A new chat opens. Any message you were drafting in your current chat stays where it was.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Tell Ari what the Skill should do">
    Ari asks what the Skill should help with. Describe the workflow, paste instructions you already have, or attach a Markdown file.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Review the saved Skill">
    Ari saves the Skill and confirms its name, when it activates, and that it is shared with your workspace. Select **View skill** in Ari's reply to read the saved instructions in **Settings → Skills**.
  </Step>
</Steps>

You can also ask Ari to save a Skill from any chat. This works well right after Ari finishes a task you want repeated, such as "Save how you built this board report as a Skill."

Every Skill has three parts:

* **A name** — lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, like `board-report`.
* **A trigger condition** — when the Skill should activate, for example "Use when the user asks for a board or investor report."
* **Instructions** — the full workflow: the steps, structure, and conventions Ari follows once the Skill activates.

A good trigger condition is specific enough that Ari doesn't activate the Skill for unrelated requests, but general enough to catch the different ways someone might phrase the same ask.

## Write a Skill yourself

To write a Skill without Ari, open **Settings → Skills** and select **Write manually**. A form opens for the name, trigger condition, and instructions. Saved Skills appear in the same list, with a search field and an **Edit** action.

## Update or remove a Skill

Ask Ari to update a saved Skill's description or instructions, or to delete one you no longer need, or do the same from **Settings → Skills**. Saved Skills belong to the workspace: everyone's conversations with Ari can activate them. Built-in Skills can't be edited or deleted — if a built-in Skill needs to work differently for your workspace, ask Ari to save a new one with a different name instead.

## Sample custom Skill prompts

These are complete, ready-to-save Skills. To use one, select **Build with Ari**, paste its instructions, and ask Ari to save it under the name in the table.

| Name                             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Instructions                                                              |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| three-statement-buildout         | Build a saved page with native Income Statement, Cash Flow Statement, and Balance Sheet tables using the workspace's existing variables, formulas, and mappings. Use when creating or updating the full three-statement model, or when auditing subtotals, cash continuity, and the balance check. | See [instructions](#three-statement-buildout-instructions) below.         |
| forecast-simulator               | Build an interactive forecast tool whose scenario ties exactly to the model baseline. Use for what-if pages, scenario explorers, or any page with controls over model variables.                                                                                                                   | See [instructions](#forecast-simulator-instructions) below.               |
| headcount-from-capacity          | Model headcount as a ratio to the business activity that sets it, not a growth rate. Use for hiring plans, workforce forecasts, personnel cost models, or org plans.                                                                                                                               | See [instructions](#headcount-from-capacity-instructions) below.          |
| interactive-profitability-bridge | Build a reusable interactive Canvas visual from the organization's existing income statement, with local preview controls that never write back to the model. Use for what-if profitability views, scenario walkthroughs of the income statement, or margin bridges.                               | See [instructions](#interactive-profitability-bridge-instructions) below. |

### `three-statement-buildout` instructions

  # Three statement buildout

  Build a saved page titled "9. Financial Statements" with three native model tables:

  1. Income Statement
  2. Cash Flow Statement
  3. Balance Sheet

  Use the workspace's existing variables, formulas, dimensions, mappings, source data, accounting conventions, currency, signs, scenario, and Last close. Do not assume USD, tax rates, fiscal years, or literal variable names. Resolve the closest verified existing variables and formulas first. Reuse existing model objects instead of creating duplicates.

  Use the current scenario unless another is specified. Preserve unrelated pages, tables, variables, formulas, mappings, scenarios, and time settings. If the page or tables already exist, update them in place.

  Use variables on rows and the system Date dimension by month across columns. Use a visible window from January 2025 through December 2030 unless another window is requested. Preserve the scenario's existing Last close and label Actuals and Forecast according to that boundary.

  ## Income Statement rows

  Use verified organizational equivalents where necessary:

  - Revenue
  - Cost of Revenue
  - Gross Profit
  - Gross Margin
  - Technology and Infrastructure
  - Sales and Marketing
  - General and Administrative

  - Operating Income

  - Adjusted Net Income

  ## Cash Flow Statement rows

  - Net Income
  - Depreciation and Amortization
  - Stock-Based Compensation Expense
  - Customer Prepayments Received

  - Change in Deferred Revenue

  - Operating Lease ROU Assets

  - Total Debt

  - Total Liabilities

  - Existing saved tables and layouts
  - Variables, formulas, source metadata, formats, currencies, and preferred time bindings
  - Dimensions, items, reporting grain, ranges, and Last close
  - Existing account mappings and statement formulas

  - Use native editable tables, not read-only Canvas tables.
  - Use the system Date axis, not a source date column.
  - Preserve source signs exactly.
  - Preserve currencies, units, decimal precision, and number formats.
  - Preserve Actuals and Forecast logic.

  - Use closing-value behavior for balance-sheet stocks such as Cash Balance.
  - Calculate margins only when the denominator exists and is nonzero.
  - Do not invent tax rates or unsupported relationships.

### `forecast-simulator` instructions

<Accordion title="View and copy instructions">
  ```markdown expandable wrap theme={null}
  # Forecast simulator

  ## The property that matters
  At default slider settings the simulated series must sit **exactly** on the baseline. If
  it drifts, every delta the user reads is contaminated by model error and the tool loses
  credibility.

  Two ways to achieve it, in order of preference:

  **A. Re-run the recurrence.** Rebuild the series in component code using the model's own
  inputs and the scenario control. At the control's default value this reproduces the model
  exactly because it is the same recurrence:

      const mwS = [];
      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (i === 0) { mwS.push(mwB[0] || 0); continue; }
        const contPrev = (contB[i-1] || 0) * Math.pow(live.contract, i-1);
        mwS.push(mwS[i-1] + Math.max(0, contPrev - mwS[i-1]) * live.act);
      }

  **B. Ratio against baseline.** Where a recurrence is impractical, scale the baseline by
  the ratio of scenario to default:

      const g = ((1 + live.traffic) * (1 + live.price)) / ((1 + D.traffic) * (1 + D.price));
      const sim = base[i] * Math.pow(g, i);

  At defaults `g === 1`, so `sim === base`.

  Read cost rates, life, and load factors from a `rates` dataset rather than hardcoding, so
  the component stays in sync when the model changes.

  ## Dataset rules
  - **One breakdown per dataset.** Multiple variables each broken down by the same dimension
    in a single dataset collapses the duplicate child labels — you get the totals and one set
    of children, and the rest render blank. Split into one dataset per variable.
  - Max 8 datasets per block. Check `dataset_evidence` in the write receipt: `series_count`
    and `series_names` tell you what actually came back.
  - A series with empty `segments` is the variable **total**; populated `segments` are
    breakdown members. Filter to `segments.length` before stacking, or the total
    double-counts against its children.
  - `layout.rows` become series; `layout.columns` (Date) become plotted points.

  ## Component contract
  - `Block({ data, state, emit })`. React and its hooks are lexical bindings — no imports,
    no `window.React`.
  - `Slider` fires `onChange(v)` for a local draft and `onCommit(v)` for an accepted change.
    **Persist only on commit** via `emit({ type: "setState", patch: { key: v } })`.
  - Sliders must never write to the model. The scenario is a local preview.
  - Provide a reset that restores defaults and clears saved state (`patch` values to `null`).
  - Show a status pill so the viewer always knows whether they're looking at baseline or a
    scenario.

  ## After writing
  Saving a Canvas block does not check that it renders. Always run `validate_code_blocks` on the
  block id — it renders in Chromium in light and dark and returns real runtime errors. Fix
  anything it reports before calling the work done.

  ## Chart selection
  Before shipping charts, check whether any two are the same curve rescaled. If per-unit
  economics are uniform across a dimension, then "units by dimension", "revenue by
  dimension", and "profit by dimension" are one shape drawn three times. Replace duplicates
  with **ratios that diverge** — cost as % of revenue, support headcount per 100 units,
  profit per employee. A quotient of two things growing at different rates carries
  information a level chart cannot. Every chart must have an explicit, descriptive title
  inside the chart configuration.
  ```
</Accordion>

### `headcount-from-capacity` instructions

<Accordion title="View and copy instructions">
  ```markdown expandable wrap theme={null}
  # Headcount from capacity

  ## Why not a growth rate
  A monthly hiring rate compounds. Fitting one to a fast-growth year and running it 48
  months produces absurd totals — a 7.7%/month rate that matches one year of real hiring
  yields 30,000 employees four years out.

  Anchor headcount to whatever the business actually scales on: megawatts, stores,
  shipments, accounts, ARR.

  ## Structure

      `Headcount per Unit` [Department]  — input, seeded at the first period
      `Headcount` [Department] = `Headcount per Unit` * `Total Units`$[Date.Month = this.Date.Month]
      `Average Salary` [Department]      — input constants
      `Personnel Cost` [Department] = `Headcount` * `Average Salary` / 12 * `Payroll Load Multiplier`

  `Headcount` needs no parent/child rules — the parent computes correctly as parent-ratio ×
  units. `Personnel Cost` does: parent is a sum, children are the explicit product.

  Note the `$[Date.Month = this.Date.Month]` on the units read. The unit total lives outside
  Department space; without it, the exact-reach seed on the spine won't reach a
  Department-coordinated cell and every row reads zero.

  ## Let the ratio move
  A flat ratio understates early scaling and overstates late. Give the ratio its own
  decaying trend:

      `Ratio Growth` = `Ratio Growth`[-1] * `Ratio Decay`        // seeded positive, decay ~0.94
      `Headcount per Unit` [Dept] = `Headcount per Unit`[-1] * (1 + `Ratio Growth`$[Date.Month = this.Date.Month])

  This reproduces a hiring surge early and flattens into operating leverage later, without
  exploding. Tune the seed to hit year-1 actuals and the decay to keep the terminal ratio sane.

  ## Diagnostics worth surfacing
  - **Revenue per employee** — sanity check against comparables.
  - **Units per employee** — the productivity trend.
  - **Support ratio** (corporate heads per 100 units) — whether the org is outgrowing what
    it serves.
  - **Profit per corporate employee** — returns on overhead headcount. This one often
    declines, and saying so is more useful than hiding it.

  ## Reconcile to the P&L
  If the P&L carries labor as a % of revenue, either drive that line from this build
  (`Units * Cost per Unit`) or add an explicit reconciliation row showing the implied
  percentage. Never let a bottom-up headcount plan sit beside a top-down labor percentage
  with no tie between them.
  ```
</Accordion>

### `interactive-profitability-bridge` instructions

<Accordion title="View and copy instructions">
  ```markdown expandable wrap theme={null}
  # Interactive profitability bridge

  Create a custom workspace skill called `interactive-profitability-bridge`.

  The skill should create or update a reusable interactive Canvas visual based on the organization's existing income statement. It should work across different organizations and must not assume specific line-item names such as Subscription Revenue, Total COGS, Gross Profit, EBIT, or Net Income.

  ## When the skill runs

  1. Inspect the current page, saved income statement tables, variables, formulas, dimensions, mappings, reporting grain, currency, and Last close.
  2. Identify the organization's available equivalents for:
     - Revenue or total income
     - Direct costs or cost of sales
     - Gross profit or contribution profit
     - Operating expenses
     - Operating profit or EBIT
     - Pretax profit
     - Tax expense
     - Net income or net profit
  3. Prefer variables already used by the organization's saved income statement.
  4. Preserve the organization's actual labels, formulas, accounting signs, currency, number formats, dimensions, and Actuals/Forecast logic.
  5. If a stage is unavailable, omit it instead of inventing a value. Do not use generic tax rates, hardcoded currencies, or assumed financial categories.

  ## Canvas block

  Create a saved Canvas block titled "Interactive Income Statement Funnel" or an equivalent organization-specific title.

  The Canvas visual should:

  - Connect to a live dataset containing the supported statement variables and system Date.
  - Allow the user to select an available reporting period at the statement's existing grain.
  - Identify the selected period as Actuals or Forecast using Last close.
  - Show supported profitability stages in order:
    - Top-line revenue or income
    - Gross or contribution profit
    - Operating profit
    - Pretax profit
    - Net income or net profit
  - Display each stage's organization-specific label, value, percentage of the top-line measure, proportional bar, and change from baseline when a preview is active.
  - Distinguish missing values from zero.
  - Display losses and negative values honestly.
  - Show a useful empty state when no supported periods or values are available.

  ## Preview controls

  Add local, non-persisted preview controls only when the required model stages exist:

  - Increase revenue or income
  - Reduce direct costs
  - Reduce operating expenses

  The controls should:

  - Start at zero.
  - Use bounded sliders with clear labels.
  - Use the organization's terminology.
  - Recalculate downstream supported stages using the same relationships as the income statement.
  - Preserve non-operating income and expense unless a specific control exists for them.
  - Preserve the selected period's tax treatment when tax is available.
  - Omit unsupported controls or outputs.
  - Include a reset-to-baseline action.
  - Never write values, formulas, assumptions, or scenario changes to the model.

  Show local impact summaries for supported outputs, such as top-line, gross or contribution profit, operating profit, and net income. Clearly label these as local preview impacts, not approved forecasts or model changes.

  ## Components and state

  Use cfo.ai Canvas components and theme tokens. Use injected components such as Select, Slider, Button, Card, Text, NumberText, Delta, and appropriate chart or visualization components. Do not use hardcoded USD formatting, a 21% tax rate, FY2026, company-specific variable names, replacement color palettes, or native HTML controls where an injected component is available.

  Store only presentation state in Canvas state, such as the selected period and preview-control values. Keep actual model data read-only.

  ## Validation

  After saving, validate the Canvas block in light and dark themes. Test:

  - Baseline values with all controls at zero
  - Period selection
  - Actuals and Forecast labeling
  - Each enabled preview control
  - Negative profit or loss
  - Missing optional stages
  - Missing values versus zero
  - Reset behavior
  - Confirmation that no model values or formulas changed

  ## Final report

  In the final response, report the saved Canvas block, the variables mapped to each profitability stage, omitted stages, preview assumptions, and any unresolved ambiguity or data gap.
  ```
</Accordion>
