{"complete":true,"content":"# Schedule recurring work with Triggers

> Have Ari run a saved instruction on a schedule, unattended, without you asking each time.

A **Trigger** is a saved instruction Ari runs by itself on a schedule, like a weekly variance summary sent to you every Monday morning, without you needing to ask each time.

## Create a Trigger

Ask Ari to schedule one, giving it:

* **A name** you'll recognize later.
* **A prompt** — phrased as a normal request, since it runs unattended and has to stand on its own without the rest of your conversation for context.
* **A schedule**, including your timezone when you specify a local time. Ari converts it to the schedule format it stores internally.
* **A delivery destination**: your Slack direct messages or your verified email address. Ari asks you to choose before it creates or updates a Trigger.

A Trigger starts enabled as soon as you create it.

<Note>
  Trigger schedules use a fixed UTC time. A Trigger set for a particular local
  time may shift by an hour when daylight saving time changes.
</Note>

## What a delivered email looks like

An email from a Trigger is formatted, not plain text. Headings, bold text, bullet and numbered lists, tables, and links in Ari's message render in the email, so a weekly variance summary can arrive as a short table with a link back to the Page. Raw HTML and images are not rendered. A Slack direct message uses Slack's own formatting.

## Pause, resume, or change a Trigger

Ask Ari to list your Triggers, or, as a workspace administrator, choose **Manage triggers** from the account menu at the bottom of the sidebar to open a chat about them, then:

* **Pause** one without deleting it, and **resume** it later.
* **Update** its name, prompt, or schedule.
* **Delete** it once you no longer need it.

You can only see and manage your own Triggers, not another workspace member's.

## Check whether a Trigger ran

Ask Ari to show a Trigger's last run. Two timestamps matter, and they answer different questions:

* **Last dispatch** records that the scheduler attempted or started a run, with its status and any error. It does not mean the work finished.
* **Last succeeded** is the only proof that a run completed.

If a run is still going when the next one is due, the overlapping run can be skipped, so a missing dispatch is not necessarily a failure. When a Trigger's job is to refresh a data connection, its run succeeds only if the import it started completes; an earlier import on the same connection does not count.

## What makes a good Trigger prompt

Because a Trigger fires with no conversation around it, write the prompt as if you were asking Ari cold: name the Table Block, Page, or Variable involved, and be specific about what you want back, like "Summarize the variance between Actuals and Forecast for Operating Expense over the last closed month, flag anything over 10%, and send the summary to my Slack direct messages."

Ari can deliver results only to your own Slack direct messages or verified email. It cannot post a scheduled update to a shared Slack channel or message another person. When Ari reports that a notification was sent, it means the email provider or Slack accepted the message; the activity card reads **Notification request accepted**, or **Notification outcome unconfirmed** when the provider gave no answer, and inbox placement is not confirmed. Each run also saves a record of what it did to Ari's memory, and the next run of the same Trigger reads those records newest first, as they were written, so a weekly summary can say what changed since last week. It also cannot complete work that requires your approval during the run, such as merging or deleting a Scenario.

{"complete":true,"content":"# Agent instructions

> Help a user connect the cfo.ai MCP server, complete browser-based authentication, select the correct workspace, and work safely.

You are helping a user connect cfo.ai to an external AI client. The cfo.ai MCP server exposes the same workspace tools Ari uses, including tools that can read and change a live financial Model.

You can configure the MCP client. The user completes account creation, sign-in, any required plan setup, and browser-based authorization. A connection is complete only when the client lists the server and can use an authorized cfo.ai tool.

## Confirm account access

Ask whether the user can already sign in to [app.cfo.ai](https://app.cfo.ai). If they cannot, direct them to create or access their account and complete any required setup in the browser.

Wait for the user to finish browser-only steps. Never ask for their password, verification code, payment details, or authorization token.

## Register the MCP server

The production server URL is:

```text theme={null}
https://api.cfo.ai/mcp
```

For Claude Code:

```bash theme={null}
claude mcp add --transport http cfoai https://api.cfo.ai/mcp
```

For Codex:

```bash theme={null}
codex mcp add cfoai --url https://api.cfo.ai/mcp
```

For another client, add `https://api.cfo.ai/mcp` as a remote HTTP MCP server named `cfoai`.

If you cannot execute a setup command, give the matching command to the user and wait for them to complete it.

## Complete browser authentication

The user approves the connection in a browser while signed in to cfo.ai.

* In Claude Code, restart the session if needed, open `/mcp`, select `cfoai`, and choose **Authenticate**.
* In Codex, run `codex mcp login cfoai` and approve the connection in the browser.
* In another client, follow its normal OAuth or remote-MCP authorization flow.

## Verify the connection and workspace

Confirm that the client lists `cfoai` and exposes its tools. A user with one workspace can usually use that workspace automatically. If the user has access to more than one workspace, call `list_orgs` and pass the intended workspace's ID or slug as `org_id` on subsequent calls.

Use a read-only inspection call to verify access before reporting success. If the client does not see the newly registered server, restart the session and check its MCP server list again.

## Understand the Model before changing it

The MCP connection provides cfo.ai's modeling instructions during initialization. Read them first. Before creating or changing model logic, call `inspect_skills` with its `list` block to find the `build-model` skill, then its `instructions` block to read it. Use `inspect_pages`, `inspect_table_blocks`, `inspect_dimension_mappings`, and `inspect_scenarios` to understand the existing workspace before creating or changing content.

The important mental model is:

* A workspace contains a financial Model, Pages, Scenarios, Variables, Dimensions, and connected data.
* Main is the primary working Scenario. Use a different Scenario when the user wants a saved alternative.
* `inspect_pages`, `inspect_table_blocks`, `inspect_dimension_mappings`, and `inspect_scenarios` read the existing Model.
* `edit_table_blocks` creates and changes visible saved tables, including their Variables, Dimensions, and formulas. Every model formula is written through it.
* `edit_pages`, `edit_dimension_mappings`, and `edit_scenarios` change Pages, Dimension mappings, and Scenarios.
* `inspect_canvas_library` and `edit_canvas_blocks` read the Canvas component library and create or update Canvas blocks, the charts and custom visuals on a Page.
* Write operations apply to the user's live Model and must match the user's request and workspace access.

## Shape each call as one action block

A multi-action tool takes exactly one block named for the action, with that action's fields inside it. There is no flat `action` field. For example, read a saved table with `inspect_table_blocks`:

```json theme={null}
{ "read": { "target": "Operating Plan" } }
```

and set a row's formula with `edit_table_blocks`:

```json theme={null}
{
  "update": {
    "target": "Operating Plan",
    "row_updates": [
      {
        "rows": ["Gross Margin"],
        "default_formulas": { "forecast": { "formula": "iferror(`Gross Profit` / Revenue, 0)" } }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

A row on a dated table takes `default_formulas` with `actuals`, `forecast`, or both; a row on a timeless table takes `formula`. Several dependent tables can go in one `create` as a `tables` list. A `delete` that lists `variables` or `dimensions` removes only those objects; when other formulas, blocks, or settings read one, the delete is refused until `force: true` is set, on the delete to cover every listed entry or on one entry to cover that entry alone. Fields that every action accepts, such as `scenario`, sit beside the block, and `scenario` is also accepted inside it. Copy names and `Name#hex` references from an inspection result instead of inventing IDs. See [Create and update formulas as an agent](/formulas/agent-docs/create-and-update) for the full shapes.

A Canvas block is named in the call that makes it: `edit_canvas_blocks` `create` requires `page`, `title`, and `source`. The reference the receipt prints, such as `Pipeline by stage#a74`, keeps naming the block in later `edit_pages` calls even after a rename. Before writing a Canvas block, call `inspect_canvas_library` with a `list` block whose `query` is a few search words, such as `"slider chart kpi"`; an entry matches when any one word appears in its title, description, tags, or aliases. Then `read` the entries you plan to use. One `read` takes up to 16 targets, so a template and the components it needs come back in one call. A Canvas write that no browser rendered returns a `render_unverified` warning naming `validate_code_blocks`, the tool that renders saved blocks in a browser and reports errors and a screenshot; a write sent with `validate: true` carries that browser result under `validation` instead. The result's `observed` sentence states what the check saw: each block rendered once per theme, with its saved state, in a 1200 px wide frame, so clicks, typing, links, and guide launches did not run and the layout at other widths is unseen. One call renders up to 8 blocks; a batch that reads a lot of calculated data is split into several renders, a single block over 20 MiB of data is refused by name, and a render run that failed returns the error code `browser_validation_unavailable` with `transient: true` and a message that names the validator stage that failed and the error behind it, so the same call can be sent again. To change part of a saved block, `edit_canvas_blocks` `update` takes `source_patches`, a list of exact `old` to `new` text replacements applied in order, each of which must occur exactly once; the block saves only when every patch applies, and `source` replaces the whole component instead. A Canvas `navigate` accepts a page or block reference in the form tool results return, and opens it the way a link chip does. `inspect_history` `changelog` takes `search` to find entries by text in the headline or in the names of the objects they changed, newest first, and reports how many entries it read in `entries_searched`. A dataset row carries each Variable's own value: a finite number, text, an ISO day such as `2026-01-30` for a date, `"true"` or `"false"` for a boolean, and `null` for an empty cell or a calculation error. Source may name a fixed color; the write saves it and its result's `source_notes` names the first one and says that colors from `theme.tokens`, `theme.design`, or `--cb-*` CSS variables follow the viewer's light or dark mode instead.

In `edit_pages`, a block action names its page with `page`; `add_text` may omit it, adding to the page in view instead, and is refused with "no target page" when nothing is in view. `reorder_blocks` still takes the page it arranges as `target`.

## Troubleshoot access

* If `cfoai` is missing, restart the client and check whether the server registration succeeded.
* If browser authentication fails, confirm that the user is signed in to the intended cfo.ai account and has access to the intended workspace.
* If tools report authorization errors after a previous success, repeat the client's authentication flow.
* If a workspace is ambiguous, call `list_orgs` and pass the intended workspace as `org_id`.","content_scope":"full_page","record_type":"documentation","target":"agent-instructions","type":"text","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/agent-instructions"}

{"complete":true,"content":"# Validate and verify formulas as an agent

> Use supported dry-run writes to validate formulas, inspect write outcomes, and verify the financial result on a saved Table Block.

Validation checks formula syntax and semantic references before a write. Verification checks whether the resulting values match the business rule.

## Validate

Use `dry_run: true` with the write that would own the actual change:

* Use `edit_table_blocks` `update` for a visible saved table target.
* Use `edit_table_blocks` `update` with a `variables` entry, and no table `target`, for a rule saved on the Variable itself.

Validation checks:

* Expression syntax
* Condition syntax
* Variable references
* Function names and arguments
* Semantic compatibility

Correct reported errors before applying the same intended change.

## Read after writing

Inspect the write result. A table write applies all requested changes together or applies none, and its receipt reports:

* Each row and column touched, with the formula it now carries per range.
* `formula_warning` issues for rules that saved but need attention: an imported Variable read in Forecast months, a constant that matches no Dimension item, a tie with an existing rule, a shared formula the write replaced, a read that lands on the generated default (0, or null for a date or text Variable) because the input lacks one of the read's coordinates, or a default saved at a grain coarser than the Model's base grain. A `create` reports the same cases as `creation_warning`. A date used as a lookup key against a Dimension of timestamps is not reported when a member sits at that day's midnight and every member of the Dimension comes from its source rows, because the engine then selects that member; a Dimension with its own member list or formula keeps exact matching, and the same date in a condition is still reported.
* One `read_note` per imported source that the written rules read, stating where that source's rows sit on the calendar and which rules read it, and one for the first Forecast month when the rule reads a prior period, a source, or a Variable with no value there, stating what the rule computed and what each read returned. A note describes the read the rules asked for, not a problem to fix.
* A `scenario_warning` naming the Scenario the write used when the call omitted `scenario`.
* A `default_rollup` issue naming the time rollup each new dated row received, and a statement of the level defaults a breakdown's save wrote or removed.
* Each default rule's scope: its condition, its range, `Date grain: <grain>` when the rule is dated, and its reach. `includes additional dimensions` means a `[...]` condition also covers cells that carry more business Dimensions, at the same Date grain; `this grain only` means an exact `$[...]` condition. A Month rule never covers Day cells, so a daily forecast needs a Day rule of its own.
* A refusal, with the field that caused it, when nothing was saved. A receipt whose `status` is `rejected` or `blocked` saved nothing and carries the same `error` object a refusal carries, beside `items[].reason`. A refusal that fits no branch of a union names the one field or shape that was wrong, and a refusal from the calculation service names the formula it was checking.

Ask for a readback in the same call with `readback.rows` and `readback.columns` to see the calculated values without a second read.

The receipt arrives before an optional readback can consume the caller's deadline. After the write commits, attribution and readback share one budget of at most 30 seconds that ends two seconds before the caller's deadline. A write whose readback did not finish reports the outcome `committed_with_readback_unavailable` with its saved revision: the change is saved and must not be sent again.

An `edit_table_blocks` write that does not answer within the runtime's deadline returns a message naming the call's `tool_call_id`. Every changelog entry the write commits records that id in the Scenario the call wrote, and `inspect_history` `changelog` entries carry `tool_call_id`, so the outcome can be read back. The server rolls back a write that has not committed within two minutes of receiving it, so two minutes after the timeout the write has either committed in full or saved nothing.

A call that repeats an earlier call exactly, after the earlier result already answered it, is refused by the runtime with the code `repeated_no_progress` and `state_changed: "no"`. The refusal is a result to act on, not a transport failure: change the request, or use what the earlier result returned.

## Verify calculated behavior

Use `inspect_table_blocks` on the relevant saved table after a material change. Check representative dates, segments, formula origins, and source information.

Every `read` result carries `calculation.source`, which says how its values were obtained: `cached`, `promoted`, `derived`, `seeded`, `full`, or `recalculated`. When a value disagrees with what the user sees, with another read, or with arithmetic you can check, and the source is anything but `full` or `recalculated`, read once more with `recalculate: true`. That read calculates the table from scratch, ignoring every cached or reused result, makes the fresh result the cached one so the page shows it too, and reports in `recalculated` whether the cached result differed and how many cells. It needs `comparison: "none"`, costs a full calculation, and is not for routine reads.

Examples:

* Compare Gross Profit with Revenue minus Cost of Goods Sold
* Check a Department formula for two different departments
* Check both sides of Last close for a formula-range change.
* Compare the intended Scenario with the Scenario that was written.

## Report clearly

State what was written and whether verification matched the request. Disclose any inferred table, Scenario, or business assumption that materially affects the result.","content_scope":"full_page","record_type":"documentation","target":"formulas/agent-docs/validate-and-verify","type":"text","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/formulas/agent-docs/validate-and-verify"}

{"complete":true,"content":"# Ari prompts

> Match a plain-language prompt to the visual Ari should build — line, bar, stacked, waterfall, funnel, gauge, or scorecard — plus prompts for tables, forecasts, Scenarios, and scheduled work.

Ari builds a different thing depending on how you ask. The same numbers can become a trend line, a stacked composition, a bridge that explains a change, or a single headline figure — and the right choice depends on the question you're asking, not on the data. Each table below pairs a plain-language prompt with what Ari should produce.

Naming the shape you want is the fastest way to get it. "Show me revenue" is ambiguous; "show me revenue by month as a line" is not.

For how to frame the question itself — the decision, the period, the level of detail — see [Ask Ari better questions](/ari/ask-better-questions).

## Choose the right visual

| When your question is                         | Ask Ari for                          |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| How has this moved over time?                 | A line chart                         |
| How do these categories compare?              | A bar chart                          |
| How much accumulated, and when?               | An area chart                        |
| What is this total made of, month by month?   | A stacked bar or stacked area chart  |
| Is our mix shifting, regardless of size?      | A 100% stacked chart                 |
| What was the split in one period?             | A pie or donut chart                 |
| Where do we lose people between stages?       | A funnel chart                       |
| What explains the change from A to B?         | A waterfall chart                    |
| How does a total compare against a rate?      | A combo chart, with bars and a line  |
| How close are we to a target?                 | A gauge, or a scorecard with a delta |
| What are the few numbers I check daily?       | A scorecard grid                     |
| What if this assumption changed?              | A chart with an interactive control  |
| I need the actual numbers in rows and columns | A Table Block, not a chart           |

## Trends over time

| Ari prompts                                                  | Ari results                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Show me revenue by month as a line."                        | A line chart of Revenue across months, on the current Page, resolved in the Scenario you are viewing.    |
| "Plot revenue and expenses on the same chart."               | One line chart with two series and a legend, sharing a time axis.                                        |
| "Show cumulative cash collected this year as an area chart." | An area chart, where the filled magnitude is the point rather than the month-to-month wiggle.            |
| "Compare this year against last year on one chart."          | Two series on the same time axis so the shapes sit on top of each other.                                 |
| "Show revenue as bars with gross margin percent as a line."  | A combo chart: revenue bars on one scale, margin percent as a line on its own scale.                     |
| "Make that quarterly instead of monthly."                    | The chart rebuilt at the coarser period and recalculated, rather than a monthly series visually thinned. |

## Composition and mix

| Ari prompts                                                            | Ari results                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Show our revenue mix as stacked bars by customer segment."            | A stacked bar chart splitting Revenue by segment, each segment its own series, stacking to the total.      |
| "Same chart, but show each segment as a share of the total."           | A 100% stacked chart, so mix shift is visible even while the total grows.                                  |
| "Break operating expense down by department over the last six months." | A stacked chart with departments as the composition and months as the axis.                                |
| "What was our revenue split by region last quarter?"                   | A pie or donut chart of that one period. A pie shows a single period's split, so name the period you mean. |
| "Show the same split as a bar chart instead."                          | The categories as bars, which is easier to compare precisely than slices.                                  |
| "Show only the segments, not the total."                               | The composition series alone, with the parent total excluded rather than double-counted.                   |

<Note>
  A pie or donut chart shows one period. If you want composition *over* time, ask for stacked bars or a stacked area chart instead.
</Note>

## Explaining a change

| Ari prompts                                                              | Ari results                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Build a waterfall explaining the change in revenue from Q1 to Q2."      | A waterfall: the opening total, the ordered signed changes that moved it, and the closing total, reconciling to the actual difference. |
| "Bridge our cash from January to June."                                  | A cash bridge of the increases and decreases between those two points.                                                                 |
| "Show what moved gross margin, from best to worst."                      | The changes ordered by size so the largest contributor reads first.                                                                    |
| "Explain the budget-to-actual gap for operating expense as a waterfall." | The variance decomposed into ordered contributions that add back to the total gap.                                                     |

<Note>
  A waterfall bridges two totals with signed changes. It is not a chart of account balances — if you want the levels themselves, ask for bars.
</Note>

## Conversion and stages

| Ari prompts                                      | Ari results                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Show our sales funnel from lead to closed won." | A funnel chart with each stage's volume, in order.               |
| "Where are we losing the most deals?"            | The stage-to-stage conversion, with the weakest step identified. |
| "Show the funnel for enterprise only."           | The same funnel filtered to that segment.                        |

## Headline numbers

| Ari prompts                                                           | Ari results                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Add a scorecard for current-quarter Revenue against target."         | A card with the headline number and its delta against target.                                  |
| "Give me a row of our five key numbers with change since last month." | A scorecard grid: each figure with its own delta, formatted in its own currency and precision. |
| "Show how close we are to our annual revenue target."                 | A gauge, or a headline figure with progress against the target.                                |
| "Add a one-line summary above this chart saying what it shows."       | A short subtitle on the chart saying what it shows.                                            |

<Note>
  A delta is colored by business meaning, not by sign. A cost coming in under plan reads as good news even though the number is negative.
</Note>

## Interactive visuals

| Ari prompts                                                     | Ari results                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Put a slider on this so I can try different hiring dates."     | A control wired to that assumption, with the outcome updating as you move it.                                                                                       |
| "Let me toggle between monthly and quarterly on this chart."    | A control that switches between two saved views of the data, remembered for that block in that Scenario.                                                            |
| "Let me try different growth rates and see the effect on cash." | An input and a live preview of the result.                                                                                                                          |
| "I like this version — save it."                                | The control's setting saved for that block. Until you save it, a control changes only your local preview, and saving a control setting never changes a Model value. |

<Note>
  A visual reads your Model but cannot write to it. Moving a slider previews an outcome; it does not change a saved assumption. To change the Model itself, ask Ari to update the Variable or formula, or edit the value in a Table Block.
</Note>

## Getting the axis and period right

| Ari prompts                                         | Ari results                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Show this weekly."                                 | The series recalculated weekly. You can ask for daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, or yearly. |
| "Drop the time axis and show the total by product." | A single-snapshot categorical chart with no date axis.                                                     |
| "Only show the last 12 months."                     | The window narrowed, with the values recalculated for it.                                                  |
| "Start the axis at zero."                           | Explicit axis bounds, overriding the default fit.                                                          |
| "Format the axis in thousands and label it."        | Compact axis formatting and a title, with the underlying values left exact.                                |
| "This chart is too short."                          | The height adjusted. Charts default to a standard height unless the content calls for more.                |

## Changing an existing visual

| Ari prompts                                       | Ari results                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Turn that line chart into stacked bars."         | The same visual and the same underlying data, redrawn in the new shape.          |
| "Narrow that chart to enterprise customers only." | The existing visual updated in place, rather than a second chart added below it. |
| "Change the title of this chart."                 | The title updated, with the data and code left alone.                            |
| "Make this one bar orange."                       | A change scoped to the element you selected, not a redesign of the whole visual. |
| "Move the cash chart above the expense table."    | The block repositioned on the Page.                                              |

## When a chart is the wrong answer

| Ari prompts                                                  | Ari results                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "I need the actual numbers behind this chart."               | A Table Block with the values in rows and columns, which you can read and edit.         |
| "Let me type next year's headcount plan in directly."        | A Table Block. Editable assumptions and recorded values belong in a table, not a chart. |
| "Show this side by side for Main and the Downside Scenario." | A Table Block with Scenario comparison columns.                                         |
| "Build a proper P\&L with subtotals."                        | A Table Block in statement structure, with subtotals that match their meaning.          |
| "Which five vendors grew the most?"                          | A named analysis table ranked to answer the question, kept as real Model state.         |

## Tables, formulas, and forecasts

| Ari prompts                                                                                 | Ari results                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Build an operating expense table by department for the last six months."                   | A Table Block with departments as rows and months as columns, reading live Model values.                                                                    |
| "Add a column comparing Actuals with Forecast and show the variance."                       | A variance Variable, actual minus plan for the same period, added to the Table Block. Built-in comparison columns compare Scenarios or periods, never both. |
| "Add a Variable for average contract value."                                                | A new Variable with its formula, placed where the rest of the Model can reference it.                                                                       |
| "Break revenue out by region."                                                              | A Dimension applied to Revenue, so it resolves per region and rolls up to the total.                                                                        |
| "Which formula applies to this cell?"                                                       | The formula that resolves there, and why that one rather than another.                                                                                      |
| "Draft the formula and check whether it is valid, but wait before applying it."             | A syntax and reference check with nothing saved, so you can review it first; the check does not calculate values.                                           |
| "Why is this row blank?"                                                                    | The reason the value doesn't resolve — a missing mapping, a formula range, or a Dimension that doesn't apply — rather than a silent zero.                   |
| "Build a 12-month revenue forecast by customer segment and label any assumptions you make." | The Variables, Dimensions, and formulas behind the forecast, with each assumption named so you can change it.                                               |
| "Build a headcount plan by department with loaded payroll cost."                            | Employee and department tables, compensation, start dates, and planned hires across time.                                                                   |
| "Build a P\&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statement that tie together."                   | A linked set of statements built from Model values and accounting records, with assumptions disclosed.                                                      |
| "Rebuild this spreadsheet in cfo.ai."                                                       | An import that reconstructs the workbook's logic as Variables and formulas, rather than loading it as source data.                                          |

## Scenarios, data, and recurring work

| Ari prompts                                                                                                  | Ari results                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| "Can we hire three engineers in September? Build a hiring Scenario and show the effect on payroll and cash." | A Scenario with the hires modeled and the effect on each outcome.                                                                                                                          |
| "What's different between this Scenario and Main?"                                                           | A summary of what actually changed, not a rebuild.                                                                                                                                         |
| "Is this Scenario ready to merge into Main?"                                                                 | What merging would change. Ask to confirm first and Ari adds a **Merge** button you press yourself; otherwise Ari can merge directly, and you can undo the merge from the version history. |
| "Connect QuickBooks Online so we can build a monthly profit and loss statement."                             | A card that opens the connection setup for you to sign in and approve. Ari cannot sign in on your behalf.                                                                                  |
| "Did the sync finish, and which periods are available?"                                                      | The connection's load status, when it last loaded, and what's ready to use.                                                                                                                |
| "Why did software spend increase last month? Break it down by vendor."                                       | The breakdown, the largest contributors, and the source records behind them.                                                                                                               |
| "Undo that last change."                                                                                     | The most recent change reverted as a whole; undo works on whole changes, not single fields.                                                                                                |
| "Every Monday, summarize last week's cash activity and send it to my Slack direct messages."                 | A named Trigger on that schedule, delivering to your own Slack direct messages or verified email. Schedules run on UTC time.                                                               |
| "Save this as our monthly close process."                                                                    | A Skill with a description of when it applies and the instructions to follow, which Ari picks up on its own next time.                                                                     |
| "Build a Guide walking a new analyst through this Page."                                                     | A saved Guide whose steps spotlight specific blocks, rows, or cells.                                                                                                                       |

## Related

* [Charts and custom visualizations](/dashboards/charts-and-custom-visualizations)
* [Ask Ari better questions](/ari/ask-better-questions)
* [Build and format a Table Block](/dashboards/build-and-format-tables)
* [Pages and blocks](/dashboards/pages-and-blocks)
* [Create and compare Scenarios](/scenarios/create-and-compare-scenarios)
* [Use cases](/use-cases)","content_scope":"full_page","record_type":"documentation","target":"ari/prompts","type":"text","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/ari/prompts"}

{"complete":true,"content":"# Workspace and team settings

> Rename your workspace, set model-wide time defaults and Last close, look up members, and invite or remove administrators.

Your workspace has a few settings that apply model-wide, rather than to any single Variable or Table Block. Ask Ari to change most of these directly.

## Rename the workspace

Ask Ari to rename your workspace. Renaming regenerates the workspace's URL slug, so any link built from the old slug changes along with it.

## Time defaults

Ask Ari to set the model's default time settings, or open **Settings → General** and use the **Date & Time** section yourself:

* **Default date granularity** — the default roll-up grain for new tables. Month unless you change it.
* **Default date range** — the default start and end date a new table shows.
* **Last close** — described below.

These are defaults for new Table Blocks; an existing table's own window (see [Build and format a Table Block](/dashboards/build-and-format-tables)) isn't affected until you change it directly.

## Last close

**Last close** is the date your Model computes Actuals against — everything at or before it is Actuals, and everything after is Forecast. Ask Ari to set it after each period closes in your books. Several other workflows, like [building a Headcount page](/headcount/build-a-headcount-page), depend on Last close being set correctly first.

## Team directory

Ask Ari to look up who is in the workspace, including current team members and pending invitations. Every member of a workspace is an administrator; there is no lower workspace role and there are no user groups. Email addresses are shown only to people with workspace-wide access-control permission. People who opened a Page through an external link are counted but not identified.

To give someone a report without making them an administrator, share the Page with an external link instead; see [Share a Page and choose its Scenario](/dashboards/share-pages-and-scenarios).

## Invite or remove workspace administrators

There is no team screen in Settings. Ask Ari, and when you have the required access it can:

* **Invite** someone as a workspace administrator. They receive an email invitation. Inviting an address whose invitation is still pending sends the email again, so ask Ari to resend rather than to cancel and re-invite.
* **Promote** an existing member to administrator. This changes their role and sends no invitation.
* **Remove** a member who has joined. Ari refuses to remove you or the workspace's last administrator.
* **Cancel** a pending invitation. Canceling and removing are separate actions: Ari refuses to cancel an invitation for someone who has already joined, and that person keeps their access, so a colleague who accepts while you are talking to Ari is never removed by mistake.

> Invite [dana@example.com](mailto:dana@example.com) to the workspace.

> Who has a pending invitation, and can you cancel the one for the old contractor?

Ari cannot invite someone with a lower role or revoke a share link. Ari can create a view-only share link to a Page; see [Share a Page and choose its Scenario](/dashboards/share-pages-and-scenarios).

## Delete a workspace or an account

There is no self-serve control for deleting a workspace or a personal account. Settings has no such action, and Ari cannot do it either. Removing a member takes away that person's access to the workspace without deleting their account.

To ask for a workspace or an account and its data to be deleted, select **Support** in the navigation at the top of these docs and name the workspace you mean. Canceling a plan is a separate step: it stops the billing and leaves the data in place. See [Billing and plan](/workspace-settings/billing).

## Related

* [Billing and plan](/workspace-settings/billing)
* [Personal theme](/workspace-settings/personal-theme)
* [Actuals, Forecast, and formula ranges](/formulas/core-concepts/actuals-forecast-and-formula-ranges)
* [Share a Page and choose its Scenario](/dashboards/share-pages-and-scenarios)","content_scope":"full_page","record_type":"documentation","target":"workspace-settings/team-and-workspace","type":"text","url":"https://docs.cfo.ai/workspace-settings/team-and-workspace"}

**Free trial**
- Terms: "Try it for free for 14 days."
- Trial access is described only as a way to "Work trial your AI CFO, for free." The page doesn't say what the trial includes.

**Startup**
- Price: $375/month billed annually; $500/month billed monthly.

  - "Standard AI Usage (limits reset monthly)"

**Growth**

entries.description:
Input constraint: Provide parameters for exactly one of: (create) or (update).

Create a Canvas visual on a page, or change an existing one: create names the page, update names the block. A dataset is a table read the block receives inverted: its layout puts the variables, with any breakdown, on rows and the shared dates or categories on columns, and each row becomes a series while each column becomes one plotted point. Each injected component's props, including Chart's options.data and options.series shape, come from inspect_canvas_library.read. Source and dataset layouts use the existing sandbox and model checks. Omitted update fields, block identity and position stay unchanged. Results include saved changes and bounded dataset checks. validate:true also returns browser validation at the saved revision; an unavailable or failed render check leaves the edit saved. validate_code_blocks checks rendering independently. In Canvas source, print() prints only that block's frame. Page ordering and removal belong to edit_pages.

_context.description: Optional active scenario, page, and time zone.

create.description: Create a Canvas block on an existing page.

after_block.description: Block name, ID, or reference immediately above the new block. Omission appends it.

page.description: The page that receives the new block, by name or as inspect_pages prints it.

source.description: Complete sandboxed React/JSX component Block({ data, timeSettings, theme, state, action, emit }); Block may accept only the supplied props it uses. React is injected as a lexical binding. Built-in hooks are reached through it, for example React.useState(...); bare useState(...) is rejected, while window.React and globalThis.React are unavailable. Injected components: BusinessDriver, Button, Card, Chart, Checkbox, Col, ControlPanel, DecisionInsight, DecisionTimeline, Delta, Divider, DriverContribution, EditableAllocation, EditableChart, Field, FunnelChart, Grid, Icon, ImpactChart, InlineButton, InteractiveFunnel, KpiCard, MetricBar, NumberText, OutcomeStrip, Pill, PreviewNotice, Radio, RadioGroup, Row, SegmentedControl, Select, Slider, Sparkline, Stat, Table, Text, TextArea, TextInput, ThresholdCrossing, Timeline, Toggle, Toolbar. Injected components cover the UI; native HTML/SVG and local components are for composing them or filling a real gap.
