source_patches.description: Exact text replacements applied in order to the current source, for focused edits that keep the rest of the source as it is. Each old must occur exactly once in the source as the earlier patches left it, and is replaced by its new. The block saves only when every patch applies. source instead replaces the whole component.

target.description: The Canvas block to change, by name, ID, or as inspect_pages prints it.

title.description: Replacement title. Absence preserves it; an empty string clears it.

validate.description: Return browser validation of the saved revision. Validation failure leaves the edit saved.

breakdownCondition.description: Restricts this later dimension to an existing ancestor dimension and member on the same path.

branch.description: The sibling path this step belongs to.

datasets.description: Live read-only datasets over existing model variables and dimensions, available as data.<name> with visible row and column layouts. On update, each entry adds a dataset or replaces the saved one with the same name, other saved datasets stay, absence preserves them all, and [] clears them all. Absent scenario selects the current scenario. Named comparisons require read access to that scenario, with at most three distinct scenarios including the selected scenario.

columns.description: Shared dates or categories; each becomes one data.<name>.rows entry. [] with window.granularity NO_GRANULARITY declares timeless scalars: one row holding each variable's value.

name.description: The identifier the block's code uses (data.<name>). Must match ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$.

scenario.description: Optional readable scenario name for a comparison dataset; absence selects the current scenario. Named comparisons are unavailable in historical snapshots. Missing or inaccessible scenarios fail without substitution.

window.description: Dataset periods and grain. Absence selects the workspace default.

end.description: Last date shown as YYYY-MM-DD, paired with start.

granularity.description: Grain of generated reporting periods. NO_GRANULARITY generates none; a Date axis then contains only dates present in source data and no dates for formula-only values.

start.description: First date shown as YYYY-MM-DD, paired with end.

layout.description: One visible axis entry. A variable may have a shared breakdown prefix, sibling branches, and an after_branches suffix. Each complete path is prefix + one branch + suffix. Standalone branches form a shared grouping axis.

branches.description: Sibling paths as one list of steps. Each step names its path with branch; steps with the same branch number form one path in list order, and paths are ordered by number. The layout compiler refuses fewer than two or more than ten paths, and a path of more than ten steps.

variable.description: Existing model variable to read. Dataset declarations select saved objects.

scenario.description: Scenario to use. Defaults to the scenario in view, which can change between turns.

schema1.description: The page the block is on. When given, confirms the block still belongs to it.

new.description: The replacement text; empty removes the matched text.

old.description: The exact source text to replace.

schema3.description: Visible child members. Their list order does not change display order or the parent measure's population.

input_schema.description: Fill exactly one action block: create, update. Fields beside the block apply to it: scenario, validate.

entries.name: mcp__cfoai__edit_pages
entries.description:
Input constraint: Provide parameters for exactly one of: (add_text) or (create) or (create_share_link) or (delete) or (delete_block) or (move) or (reorder_blocks) or (share) or (update) or (update_text).

Creates, renames, moves, shares, and deletes pages; sets page icons; adds and edits text; reorders and removes blocks. A moved page takes its subpages with it. A deleted page loses its blocks; its subpages move up to its parent and keep their audience. New top-level pages are private and subpages follow their parent; changing a page's audience or parent previews the access change first and needs the user's approval. inspect_pages reports page_audiences_enabled; in a workspace where it is false, update can also reparent a page directly without a preview. create_share_link adds page READ in one scenario; existing grants stay effective. Its receipt describes access and revocation. target names the page or block an action changes; each block action names its page with page. Blocks keep their identity, settings, and position unless moved. Edits return the saved order and an undoable change; links leave the model unchanged. Canvas content belongs to edit_canvas_blocks; modeled tables belong to edit_table_blocks.

_context.description: Optional active scenario, page, and time zone.

add_text.description: Add a text block to an existing page; Markdown carries formatted prose. A text block is one column of prose; side-by-side and grid layouts, including their narrative cells, are Canvas blocks.

after_block.description: Block name immediately above the new block. Absence appends to the page.

create.description: Create a page and its initial narrative blocks in one change. The sidebar and header show the page as its icon and name, in the icon and icon_color saved with it.

icon.description: The icon shown beside the page name in the sidebar and header: a plain picture of what the page is about, which a person recognizes at a glance and which tells the page apart from the pages around it. Described in a few words ("truck", "bar chart", "office building") or as a catalog icon id. The closest catalog icon is applied and reported with its runners-up. A phrase that shares no word with any catalog icon leaves the icon as it is (a new page shows the default glyph) and the receipt reports icon_matched_by "none"; the rest of the call applies. 'none' removes the icon. Null leaves it unchanged.

icon_color.description: Color for the page icon. The accent colors mark the workspace's own pages and gray is the neutral of the app's own controls. The sidebar is read as a whole, so color shows which pages belong together: a page shares the color of its parent and of pages on the same subject, and a separate subject has a color of its own. inspect_pages returns the icon and color each page has now. Null keeps the current color, or gray for a new icon.

create_share_link.description: Create an external link that adds READ grants for this page and scenario when followed, optionally opening further pages. Recipients keep existing roles and page grants, including editing rights. Returns the saved sharing URL; its receipt explains admission and revocation.

additional_pages.description: Further existing pages, by name, that this link opens besides the target, in the same scenario. The target stays the page recipients land on. Without it, the link opens one page.

delete.description: Delete a page and everything on it. Its subpages are kept and move up beside it.

delete_block.description: Remove one block from a page.

move.description: Move a page in the sidebar tree: under another page, out to the top level, or up and down among its siblings. Its subpages move with it.

after_page.description: Page immediately above it under the same destination parent. Absent places the page last; null places it first.

page_order.description: Complete top-to-bottom order within one level: every page directly under parent exactly once, by name or issued target. It cannot reparent; single-page fields change a page's parent.

to_root.description: true moves the page to the top level; mutually exclusive with parent.

org_id.description: Workspace ID or slug. Optional when you belong to one workspace. Otherwise, call list_orgs and choose an ID or slug. Numbers always identify workspace IDs.

reorder_blocks.description: Rearrange a page's blocks, or move one to another page with place.to_page. The source is page or target, the current page, or the page identified by a qualified place.block.

block_order.description: Complete top-to-bottom block order for one page, with each visible block exactly once by name or issued target. place handles a single block or a move to another page.

place.description: Move one block and leave the rest in order. to_page sends it to another page.

after_block.description: Block immediately above it on the destination page. The destination is to_page when supplied, otherwise the page selected by target or the runtime page when target is absent. Absence appends to that page; null places it first.

block.description: Block to move, by name or issued target. A name is looked up on the page named at the top level, or on its current page when to_page sends it elsewhere.

to_page.description: Existing destination page by name or issued reference. Absence keeps the block on its current page.

target.description: Name of the existing page or block to change. A target returned by an earlier result names it exactly.

scenario.description: Scenario to use. Defaults to the scenario in view, which can change between turns.

share.description: Preview or confirm who can open a page and its subpages in the selected scenario. Model data remains shared.

audience.description: private: only the current user. shared: the people named in recipients. workspace: every ordinary workspace member can edit; page owners keep full access. keep: the audience stays as it is and only the named grants change.

userId.description: An inspected existing workspace user's ID.

remove_user_ids.description: Existing workspace user IDs whose named grants on this page are removed. The preview lists each affected person's access before and after the change.

update.description: Rename a page, set its date range, or set its icon, the icon shown beside its name in the sidebar and header, separate from the name. With page audiences disabled, update can also change a legacy page's parent; otherwise a parent change goes through move, which reviews the access change.

icon.description: The icon shown beside the page name in the sidebar and header: a plain picture of what the page is about, which a person recognizes at a glance and which tells the page apart from the pages around it. Described in a few words ("truck", "bar chart", "office building") or as a catalog icon id. The closest catalog icon is applied and reported with its runners-up. A phrase that shares no word with any catalog icon leaves the icon as it is (a new page shows the default glyph) and the receipt reports icon_matched_by "none"; the rest of the call applies. 'none' removes the icon. Null leaves it unchanged.

icon_color.description: Color for the page icon. The accent colors mark the workspace's own pages and gray is the neutral of the app's own controls. The sidebar is read as a whole, so color shows which pages belong together: a page shares the color of its parent and of pages on the same subject, and a separate subject has a color of its own. inspect_pages returns the icon and color each page has now. Null keeps the current color, or gray for a new icon.

window.description: The page date range, the range its date control shows. Saving it sets the range of every table, chart, and Canvas dataset on the page; Canvas code reads dates only through its datasets. Null leaves it unchanged.

update_text.description: Update an existing text block in place without changing its ID, page, or position.

allow_access_loss.description: true accepts that the change removes the current user's own access, as the preview showed.

allow_wider_link_revocation.description: true accepts that the change revokes the share links the preview listed in other scenarios.

confirm_access_change.description: Two-step change: a call without this field returns a preview for the user to review; a call with true plus the preview's expected_revision and operation_id applies it.

content_2.description: TipTap document JSON for formatted text. A nonempty document takes precedence over text; Markdown is a separate content format.

convert_descendants.description: true accepts that the subpages the preview listed lose their own access settings and follow this page.

expected_revision.description: The value from the preview. A change to the page's audience or position since then makes it stale.

operation_id.description: The value from the preview; it ties this confirmation to that preview.

page_2.description: The page the block is on. Absence uses the page in view; an issued block target finds its own page.

parent_2.description: Parent page by name or issued reference. For create, absence creates a top-level page; a named parent prevents reuse of a same-named page elsewhere. For update, a named parent can reparent a legacy page only when page_audiences_enabled is false; omission preserves its parent.

scenario.description: Scenario to use. Defaults to the scenario in view, which can change between turns.

schema1.description: For delete: true accepts that the page's blocks are deleted with it. Omitted or false refuses a page that still has blocks and returns their list.

schema2.description: true deletes the block even when formulas or other blocks still depend on its table-owned objects; those references will break.

schema3.description: The page that receives the new block, by name or as inspect_pages prints it. Absence uses the page of an issued after_block reference, else the page in view, else the scenario's only page.

schema5.description: The page whose blocks this arranges, by name or as inspect_pages prints it. target names the same page.

schema7.description: Destination parent page by name or issued target. For a single-page move: absent or null keeps the current parent, and to_root=true moves it to the top level. For page_order: the level being reordered, absent for the top level; page_order never changes a page's parent. A page cannot move under itself or its descendants.

schema9.description: Narrative blocks to create with the page, in their visible order.

target_2.description: Name of the existing page or block to change. A target returned by an earlier result names it exactly.

text.description: Plain text; each line becomes a paragraph. Markdown is converted as in the markdown field.

input_schema.description: Fill exactly one action block: add_text, create, create_share_link, delete, delete_block, move, reorder_blocks, share, update, update_text. Fields beside the block apply to it: scenario.

entries.name: mcp__cfoai__edit_scenarios
entries.description:
Input constraint: Provide parameters for exactly one of: (create) or (delete) or (merge) or (rename) or (snapshot).

Creates, renames, snapshots, merges, or deletes scenarios. create makes an editable scenario based on Main; other scenarios can be snapshotted as pinned versions, not forked. A snapshot stops inheriting later changes, including integration syncs, but edits to it are not blocked and still save, so a snapshot does not stop anyone from changing it. Snapshots cannot be merged. merge removes the source scenario. delete removes a non-Main scenario that has no children and returns a changelog entry, so edit_history can undo it. Results identify the resulting scenario and its owner. A scenario chosen by name must be unambiguous; an ambiguous name is refused with candidates.

_context.description: Optional active scenario, page, and time zone.

delete.description: Delete an existing scenario. The returned changelog entry can restore it.

target.description: The existing scenario to delete, by name. Main and scenarios with children cannot be deleted.

merge.description: Merge a scenario into its parent. The merged scenario is removed afterward.

target.description: The existing scenario to merge, by name. Main, snapshots, and merge-disabled scenarios cannot be merged.

org_id.description: Workspace ID or slug. Optional when you belong to one workspace. Otherwise, call list_orgs and choose an ID or slug. Numbers always identify workspace IDs.

target.description: The existing scenario to rename, by name.

snapshot.description: Pin a scenario's state at a point in its history. The snapshot stops inheriting later changes, including integration syncs; edits to it still save.

at_change_log_id.description: Numeric changelog ID from inspect_history, inclusive of all changes through that entry. The preceding entry represents the state before an action.

of_scenario.description: The scenario being snapshotted, by name; defaults to the scenario in view. Cannot be a scenario that is itself a snapshot.

input_schema.description: Fill exactly one action block: create, delete, merge, rename, snapshot.

entries.name: mcp__cfoai__edit_table_blocks
entries.description:
Input constraint: Provide parameters for exactly one of: (copy) or (create) or (delete) or (reshape) or (set_time_rollup) or (update) or (update_calendar).

Creates, updates, reshapes, copies, or deletes saved tables atomically. create declares a table's rows and columns, or several tables under tables. reshape supplies the complete ordered layout; retained inspected nodes keep their identities, and omission does not delete shared model objects. update changes selected values, formulas, formatting, members, or settings without replacing the layout. Nodes declare or reuse variables, dimensions, or time axes with formulas, members, breakdowns, format, and a variable's rollup. Row and column selections can share a patch. Omitted patch fields stay unchanged; inherit removes the selected local override. delete removes the table unless variables or dimensions name shared objects to delete; force acknowledges their dependents. Variable, dimension, and source settings, set_time_rollup, and update_calendar belong to the object or scenario and need no table: scenario names the scenario (the current one when omitted), and a target only lends the receipt its view.

_context.description: Optional active scenario, page, and time zone.

force.description: For deletion, true permits removing objects with dependents, and those references break. It covers the table's own objects when the table is deleted, or every variables and dimensions entry when they select what to delete; an entry's own force covers that entry alone.

org_id.description: Workspace ID or slug. Optional when you belong to one workspace. Otherwise, call list_orgs and choose an ID or slug. Numbers always identify workspace IDs.

layout.description: Complete ordered rows and columns. Omitted nodes leave this layout, except an object's home-table node; [] clears a side. Retained nodes carry their complete inspected definitions. New nodes use the create grammar and are created and placed in this save, on either side under new or existing parents. Omitted settings, comparison and preserved remain unchanged. Shared variable and dimension settings are edited with update's variables and dimensions.

items.description: One concrete row's saved breakdown. under is its full inspected parent row; root is the one node nested there, using the same saved-node fields. ref/target is absent only when creating an entry. Other item entries and legacy interiors remain separate owners.

comparison.description: Scenario or period comparison. Omitted or null keeps the saved comparison; an object replaces it, and {} clears both kinds.

scenarios.description: Scenario names or references returned by inspect_scenarios. Each scenario must be readable. Old table-owned comparison references can preserve an already saved entry only.

preserved.description: References that a read lists for opaque legacy entries and for saved setting overrides. Accepted so a copied read can be sent back unchanged; it changes nothing, because omitted entries and settings are already kept.

remove.description: Inspected references of opaque legacy item breakdowns to remove. Entries not listed here stay saved. An editable breakdown is removed by leaving it out of breakdowns.

settings.description: Local table settings. Each omitted field keeps its saved override, {"inherit":true} releases that field to the scenario's inherited value, and a value sets it; {} keeps every setting. Top-level window, grain, and other setting fields beside layout fill omitted fields here; two different explicit values are refused. Saved widths stay unchanged. inherited_settings from a read is separate, read-only evidence.

scenario.description: Defaults to the scenario in view, which can change between turns.

method.description: SUM adds flows. LAST reads the final base period, preserving a missing closing value. AVERAGE computes the mean of base-period values.

period.description: Actuals, Forecast, or a saved range. Omit for both system ranges.

target.description: Variable name or copied inspection target.

dimensions.description: Settings and members of the named dimensions. A setting is the dimension's wherever it is read and needs no target; member edits go through a table that shows the dimension. Omitted settings are preserved; delete selects these entities explicitly.

structure.description: Insert, move, then remove nodes. Removal drops an occurrence and subtree, never its objects; an object's home-table node stays until the object is deleted. Moves retain children. Destinations use side rows/columns, optional parent, and before/after sibling references; omission appends. Inserts use the shared node grammar, and the same update may write the cells of the inserted rows or columns with cell_updates or values.

variables.description: Settings of the named variables: name, data_type, aggregation_function, preferred_time_property, format, decimal_places, currency, and default_formulas, the variable's own Actuals and Forecast rules. A setting is the variable's wherever it is read, so it lands on every variable named here, placed on this table or not, and needs no target. Omitted settings are preserved; delete selects these entities explicitly.

calendar.description: Time defaults, Last close and named formula ranges of the scenario named by scenario, the current one when omitted; every table in that scenario shares them. These are separate from a table's grain/window display overrides.

range.description: Without target it creates; with target it updates. Bounds accept dates or date-reference targets. An empty string opens an endpoint; omission/null preserves an existing bound.

add_dimension_items.description: Creates or reuses model-wide string members and attaches them to this table at their final parent. Explicit order is an ordinary sort update. values and cell_updates in this request may target new members.

dimension.description: The string dimension that breaks down this axis in the final layout, by readable property name or inspected saved-axis reference.

under.description: A complete inspected parent row or column address in the final layout. Absent only for a root grouping. Sort and member filters stay unchanged unless explicitly updated.

axis_sort.description: Order of this grouping axis's members: AXIS_ASC or AXIS_DESC by member, or MANUAL with manualOrdering naming the members that come first. The order belongs to the axis, so every parent using that axis shows it. Parent-local order requires an inspected axis owned by that complete item's breakdown; a rendered member address does not create such an owner.

based_on.description: The as_of of the table read, or the change_log_id of the table write, this edit builds on. The receipt's changed_since_read issue names what others saved to the table after that point, and who; the edit is saved either way.

breakdownBranches.description: Independent sibling paths. Each root-to-leaf path permits at most one branches fork. This explicit grouping keeps the complete published edit schema at its measured 14-level provider bound.

breakdownCondition.description: Restricts this later dimension to an existing ancestor dimension and member on the same path.

include.description: Selects visible child members. List order does not set display order; row_updates or column_updates with before/after order siblings. The parent measure population is unchanged.

dimension.description: A dimension by name or inspected reference. A name that matches one existing dimension reuses it; an unmatched name creates the dimension on this table.

cell_update.description: One rule at the selected cells' coordinates: formula or value saves it, clear_formula removes it. On a timeless row with one value column those coordinates are the row's own, so the edit writes or removes the row's formula.

clear_formula.description: Removes the rule saved at the selected cells' coordinates; with none saved there, the outcome is unchanged.

cell_updates.description: Cell rules and styles, including cells of rows, columns, members, or a table this same request creates.

childDefaults.description: The rules the cells beneath the selected row or column inherit, one entry per breakdown dimension at any depth; a deeper level's entry is saved on the level above it (Total by Owner by Deal: the Deal entry is the rule on Total[Owner]). An axis row (Total[stage]) rules every member's children; a member row (Total[Discovery]) pins that member. Levels above the deepest without their own rule sum the level beneath in its ranges.

actuals.description: The Actuals rule these children inherit, as default_formulas.actuals takes it; omitted or null is unchanged.

clear.description: true removes the owned timeless child default; dated ranges clear through actuals or forecast.

dimension.description: A dimension of this row's breakdown at any depth, by name or reference (Employee ID#28); Date is not one.

forecast.description: The Forecast rule these children inherit, as default_formulas.forecast takes it; omitted or null is unchanged.

formula.description: The timeless rule these children inherit, in the item's formula grammar; dated tables use actuals and forecast.

clearAxisFormula.description: Removes only the formula owned by this timeless selection. If none exists, the outcome is unchanged; inherited formulas remain.

clearRangeFormula.description: Removes only the formula owned by the selected business scope, Date grain, and range. With no owned formula, the outcome is unchanged. Inherited rules and exact cell overrides remain.

formula.description: The selected column's own rule on a timeless table. Dated scopes use default_formulas. The rule its children inherit goes in child_defaults on this item. Omission preserves it; clear_formula removes its owned rule.

period_range.description: Inclusive system Date interval at the saved axis grain, with bounds in that grain's period spelling, such as 2026-07 through 2026-09 for month.

coordinate_selector.description: A row or column: a ref with a # suffix, a name or path, a member by its path from its variable or axis dimension, one bracket per breakdown level, as a readback prints it (Revenue[West], Revenue[West][Enterprise], Employee ID[E-207]), a period such as 2026-03, a predicate such as `Employee ID` in any, or a period_range. The member with no value is spelled empty:None (Region[empty:None]). Backticks around a name are optional.

create_columns.description: Ordered columns using the create node grammar. An explicit empty list gives the table no column breakdown: with plain variable rows and window.granularity NO_GRANULARITY, a timeless scalar table whose one column is Value; with one plain dimension row, a member table, including an empty dimension. A dated table needs a Date column such as {"time": "MONTH"}.

anyOf.description: A table compares either across time (period_offset) or across scenarios (scenarios), never both; passing both is refused. Zero offset or an empty scenario list clears the comparison. Measures or layout alone select nothing.

layout.description: Scenario-comparison placement: COLUMNS or ROWS. Period comparison does not use this setting.

measures.description: Period comparison: CURRENT, COMPARISON_VALUE, DELTA, PERCENT. Scenario comparison: VALUE, DELTA, PERCENT. The mode-specific value names are not interchangeable.

period_offset.description: Number of earlier periods in the saved Date grain to compare with; it needs a Date axis. Zero clears the comparison.

scenarios.description: Existing scenarios to compare with, other than the selected scenario. The list replaces the saved one; an empty list clears the comparison.

create_dimensions.description: Settings of these dimensions, saved with the new table, or a new mapping into one: keys, items, and catch_all as edit_dimension_mappings map takes them, written in this change before the rows, so a rule reading the mapped dimension resolves in this call; the receipt's items entry for the dimension carries the mapping's facts. Targets use the declared name.

catch_all.description: Fixed target-wide fallback written beside the rows: records that no lookup into the target matches resolve to this item.

items.description: Single-key source values mapped to fixed reporting items. Nonempty items requires exactly one key.

keys.description: Source dimensions identifying this exact lookup.

create_rows.description: At most 100 top-level rows; formulas, variables, formatting, columns, and propagated saved records do not count. Complete ordered layout: each variable entry is a calculated value, a parent with a breakdown included, and dimension children split it into member rows. Separate variables carry a statement's lines and subtotals; successive dimensions describe the levels of a categorical breakdown. Unrelated table settings are preserved. Extend larger tables with structure updates or reshape. Empty rows and columns create an empty table.

create_variables.description: Settings of these variables, saved with the new table, placed on it or only read by its formulas: name, type, aggregation, source date, display format, and default_formulas. Targets use the declared name (net_revenue); name is the display name from this save (Net revenue).

anyOf.description: Saved display window controls visible periods; formulas can still read periods outside it. Bounds are absolute YYYY-MM-DD dates supplied together; relative date strings are not accepted.

granularity.description: NO_GRANULARITY makes the table timeless: no reporting periods and no Date axis. Any other grain gives a table that creates a new variable a Date axis.

declarativeRangeDefault.description: Declarative range default: an expression sets the owned formula, {"inherit":true} removes its owned override, and null preserves it.

formula.description: Initial formula at this variable's final scope: its ancestors, the opposite axis and the table's Date grain. Breakdown children scope only their own cells. Each inheriting cell evaluates its own inputs; literals represent constants. Example: Revenue - COGS. Full grammar: build-model / Formula syntax.

defaultFormulasEdit.description: Actuals and Forecast defaults for the selected row's or column's own rule at its variable/breakdown scope. The rule its children inherit goes in child_defaults on the same item. Each supplied range sets formula or clears its owned rule; omission preserves it and cell overrides. New defaults include finer grains; existing rules retain their scope.

defaultFormulasInitializer.description: Actuals and Forecast formulas for this row's or column's own rule, saved with the layout. One entry per variable; on an existing variable they replace its saved defaults, as an update would.

format.description: Table-default style. More specific row, column and cell styles remain unchanged. Explicit indent changes require whole-row selection; reset clears all local table-default style fields.

format_updates.description: Style patches keyed by the refs a read's formatting.scopes prints: a row or column ref for a saved node's style, or a Formatting scope#hash ref for a style no coordinate names. Calculated row and column selections remain in their existing update fields.

formula_breaks_hidden.description: Complete local list of hidden formula ranges, by name or inspected target. [] clears the list; {inherit:true} restores scenario inheritance for the whole list.

formula_groups_hidden.description: Complete local map from value-column group names or inspected references to hidden booleans. {} clears the map; {inherit:true} restores scenario inheritance for the whole map.

formula_hidden.description: Default visibility of formula columns. Group overrides and hidden ranges remain separate.

hidden.description: Hides or shows the saved axis the selection belongs to; a member row (Total[West]) names its axis, so every member of that level hides. The page hides every row and column beneath a hidden axis, whatever their own hidden says. A group's summary column hides with its group and stays when only levels beneath it hide.

hide_dimension_headers.description: true leaves out the row naming the dimension above each group of dimension items, so items sit directly under their parent row; false shows it.

include_edit_rules.description: Adds the editing rules of the touched rows and columns to the readback: accepted actions, owned defaults with ownership and writability, and formula roles. Omission returns writability alone.

nodeDataType.description: Type of the object this node declares or names. A new dimension's member type: STRING by default, DATETIME for members from the timeline; an existing dimension keeps its type. On a variable, its value type, saved as the variable's setting.

nodeFormula.description: A shared, grain-free formula with condition [], used only when this declaration creates a new variable. Dated defaults may inherit it. Same grammar and forms as default_formulas.actuals.formula.

propertyDefaultFormulas.description: The variable's own Actuals and Forecast rules, saved with no placement.

rangeFormula.description: The reusable calculation for this range. Each matching cell evaluates the expression with its own inputs. Example: Revenue - COGS. Forms: `Net Revenue` (quoted name); Revenue carries the current row's dimensions, Date included; Revenue$[...] is absolute and names its own segment; Revenue[Region="West"] reads West instead of the row's Region; Revenue[-1] is the previous period; Revenue[Region in any] spans every Region. Write ^ = <>; ** == != still parse. Full grammar: build-model skill, Formula syntax reference (inspect_skills instructions).

readback.description: Calculate selected rows and columns after the edit commits, with values, formulas, and zero or empty members hidden by the display. An omitted side reads all top-level rows or all columns. Period selection verifies only those cells and leaves the display window unchanged. Selectors follow the read grammar; renamed variables or dimensions resolve by either name. Unresolved selectors appear in issues as readback_selector_unresolved with the nearest coordinates; other selections still read. also adds other tables read at the same change. Read failure preserves the saved edit.

also.description: Other saved tables to read at the same change, so the edit's effect downstream arrives with this receipt. Each entry's result is under readback_also in request order; a target or selector that does not resolve is an issue on that entry.

columns.description: Columns of that table. Omitted reads every column.

rows.description: Rows of that table, in the selector grammar above. Omitted reads every top-level row.

target.description: A table, as a read's target names one: a name, a ref, or an id.

depth.description: Child levels to include under each selected row, or all, with the read's meaning: 1 adds each row's members, 2 their members. Omitted returns the selected rows alone.

breakdown.description: Replace this one concrete row's item-owned breakdown with one saved root; [] removes its entry. Omission preserves it. This does not replace a shared configured breakdown.

formula.description: The selected row's own rule on a timeless table. Dated scopes use default_formulas. The rule its children inherit goes in child_defaults on this item. Omission preserves it; clear_formula removes its owned rule.
A copied null reports no owned default and makes no change; clear_formula:true removes a default.

range.description: Readback evidence on a retained node; ignored by formula writes.

range_binding.description: Read-only range binding evidence on a retained node.

range_unavailable.description: Read-only unavailable-range evidence on a retained node.

savedDefaultFormulasEdit.description: Actuals and Forecast rules of the selected row, column, or variable at its scope and Date grain. Each supplied range sets a formula or clears its owned rule; an omitted range stays unchanged. The rule a row's children inherit goes in child_defaults on the same item. Existing rules keep their saved scope; a new rule takes the selected scope and reaches finer grains.

savedFormulaEvidence.description: Inspection-only evidence on a retained node; copying it does not author formulas.

savedFormulaRangeEvidence.description: Readback evidence on a retained node: the range's reference, definition, and resolved bounds as a read returned them. Writes ignore it.

breakdown.description: Levels nested beneath this variable, outermost first, as on create. Each level may declare its dimension with items and data_type and carry the sort of the axis it creates; children is the same nesting in saved-node form.

child_defaults.description: Dated actuals and forecast rules this variable's breakdown children inherit, saved with the layout for a new or existing variable; an entry may name any breakdown level, so one create row carries a total's rule and its leaf rule. formula and clear update the saved row.

items.description: A saved child node. It uses the same fields recursively; the complete recursive contract is checked before execution.

dimension.description: A dimension node shows members, by name or inspected reference, so the entry carries dimension and display settings: a breakdown lists the dimension's items, and the value axis of a record table shows the item each key row is mapped to. A saved Date axis reads as a dimension with its grain. A name matching one dimension reuses it; an unmatched name creates it here with data_type and items when given; items also extend an existing dimension. A value other tables break down by is a dimension; a value you calculate with is a variable.

filter.description: Visible members of a dimension this node declares or places. On a retained node, members is the saved filter; a node takes one of the two.

format.description: Initial style for this node's row or column, applied in the same save. Retained nodes keep their saved styles unless a field is given here.

bg.description: Background color: purple, teal, orange, yellow, red, pink, blue, green, yellow green, cyan, azure, indigo, or magenta. Corresponding DC1-DC13 tokens are also accepted, ignoring case. null, default, or DC0 clears this scope's fill and reveals inherited styling.

decimalPlaces.description: Displayed decimal places. null clears this scope's override and reveals inherited formatting; omission preserves it.

indent.description: Row indentation from 0 to 8. Applies only to row targets. null clears the row's local setting; omission preserves it.

numberFormat.description: Number display format. null clears this scope's override and reveals inherited formatting; omission preserves it.

formula.description: The timeless default expression of the selected calculated value, including a dimension shown as a value or a variable enclosing or opposite a dimension axis. This edits the calculated value's rule; a pure member-list axis cannot author a generated-member formula. Source-linked dimensions offer that authoring path to the person in the row-header menu: More settings, then Edit dimension formula. On a retained target, copied null is readback absence evidence and preserves the current default; clear_formula:true removes the owned rule. For new declarations, a supplied formula must be a string.

formulas.description: Selects a saved table's formula-column group, the axis node that holds its formula columns, when a reshape layout places it. A create column names what it shows: variable, dimension, or time.

hidden_by.description: Read-only hidden ancestor that hides this node; writes ignore it.

new.description: Create another variable with this name even when an existing variable already carries it. Within this request's layout the name then means the new variable; the existing ones stay reachable by their tokens.

ref.description: The saved node to keep, as target; a read prints it under this name.

rollup.description: How this new row's variable summarizes its base periods at each of quarter, half-year, and year that is coarser than the base grain, saved with the layout for Actuals and Forecast. SUM adds flows, LAST reads the final base period for a balance, and AVERAGE takes the mean. The receipt names each grain written, or an omitted rollup's default; set_time_rollup changes a saved rollup.

space.description: An empty row slot with no property: a blank separator row on create, or a saved slot kept for a later fill on reshape. A new property node needs no space.

target.description: The saved node to keep, by the same selector a cell write takes: the row or column ref a read or receipt printed (Revenue#7e), its nested label (Revenue[Country]), the variable or dimension it shows (Revenue#6, Country), or a member row of its breakdown (Revenue[United States]#d), which names the breakdown axis. Two placements of one variable are told apart by their refs. With variable or dimension the node keeps that object and may change settings and children. Formula fields select a calculated value: a retained dimension breakdown uses its enclosing variable and a dimension axis opposite one variable scopes that variable, and a dimension shown as a value uses the mapping/formula owner. A member-list axis with no calculated value on either side has no formula authoring operation; dimensions add_items, remove_items, replace_items, and rename_items edit saved membership; alone, the node is kept exactly as saved. Absent on a new node.

time.description: Declares a system Date axis at this reporting grain; the dimension is created when the model has none.

variable.description: The variable shown, by name or inspected reference. Unambiguous existing names reuse that object, including from another table; unmatched names create it. default_formulas and child_defaults on the row are saved with the layout for a new or an existing variable; a timeless formula on an existing variable is an update on an undated row. On a retained reshape node, supplied formulas edit its defaults and omission preserves them. new:true creates another namesake. Ambiguous names return candidates. Shows a shared variable's values, which may be numbers, text, or dates.

scenario.description: Defaults to the scenario in view, which can change between turns.

schema2.description: Validates structure, references, and formula syntax without writing; returns valid, warnings, and model_effects. No values come back, since calculation does not run, and cycles go undetected. A reshape dry run previews deleting a home-owned row or column; deleting the whole table takes no dry_run.

anyOf.description: A page name reuses a unique match or creates a page. Omission uses the current page, or creates a page named after the table when none is usable. A new page and table commit together, and two creates in one step that name the same new page share it: one receipt says the page was created, the other that it was reused.

true shows every generated row and column member, including those whose values are all zero or empty in the window; false requests hiding members whose values are all zero or empty, subject to the workspace empty-result policy. Omitted, create uses the workspace default and update keeps the saved setting.

schema27.description: Several tables in one create, saved in list order in one change: a later table's formulas name the variables an earlier table declares, and two entries naming one new page share it. The response holds one receipt per table; a refusal of any table refuses them all and names the table. The request's scenario and dry_run apply to every entry.

schema3.description: The saved member filter of the selected axis, in one of two forms. A list of member names replaces the filter, a saved condition included, and may name empty:None, the rows with no value; [] clears it. A string is a live condition the table evaluates at every calculation; it narrows the saved list. It may read a dimension mapped from the axis: Employee where Status = "Active". Region not in {"West"} keeps every named member but West; the empty member has no value, so a comparison on it is unknown and a null check inside where is what keeps it: Region where (Region = null or not (Region in {"West"})). Literals are quoted strings; a bare number is a reference offset, not a member; date and number members match by their saved rendered text, such as "2026-01-01 00:00:00+00". A member row (Total[West]) names its axis. Omission or null preserves the filter.

schema30.description: Manual members to create on this dimension, new or existing, in this request. Existing members are kept.

schema4.description: How the saved axis is used, DIMENSION or VARIABLE. Not a formula role: those are written with formula, default_formulas, and child_defaults.

schema48.description: true sets this style at this scope; false or null clears this scope's setting so broader scopes apply; omitted, it stays unchanged.

schema99.description: Optional saved table whose calendar view the receipt returns. The calendar itself belongs to the scenario named by scenario, the current one when omitted.

sources.description: The date column a source query's rows sit on, saved as preferred_time_property on every variable and dimension of that source in this write except the ones a variables or dimensions entry sets itself; target is the query reference a read prints under sources, and the column is one of the source's date columns.

style.description: Saved style changes. Omission preserves a field; {"inherit":true} removes its owned override; a text style (bold, italic, underline, strike) takes true to set and false to remove the override. reset:true removes the selected owned style.

summary.description: NONE keeps modeled parent; others combine children independently of time rollup

values.description: Literal inputs: columns and each row's first entry are single coordinate strings in the readback grammar, excluding predicates and period_range. Targets may be rows or columns inserted or declared in this request. Remaining entries give one value per column. Dated inputs leave the display window unchanged; window sets the displayed dates, and a new table's Date columns cover only dates inside it. A value saves a rule at its cell coordinates; edit_integrations ingest_csv saves a CSV as a data source. For a timeless row with one value column, these are the row's own coordinates and the value replaces its formula. null leaves its cell as it is; clear_formula in cell_updates removes a saved value.

input_schema.description: Fill exactly one action block: copy, create, delete, reshape, set_time_rollup, update, update_calendar. Fields beside the block apply to it: scenario.
